articleTitle: Study on carbonation resistance of EPS concrete based on mix proportion design
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: This paper presents a study on carbonization resistance of two mix proportions of EPS concrete with density of 1200kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Besides, the mechanism of carbonation resistance of EPS concrete is explained by SEM imaging. The results show that the carbonation resistance of EPS concrete increases obviously when mix proportion includes micro beads and silica fume, which results in carbonization depth decrease by 71.3% at 28 days. It is also found that micro beads and silica fume can reduce the harmful pores in the interface transition zone (ITZ) of EPS concrete, and enhance the compactness of cement matrix, leading to great improvement in carbonation resistance of EPS concrete. The research results of this study provide a potential reference for the selection of EPS concrete in engineering practice.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Seismic Performance Evaluation of Existing Buildings through Non-stationary Stochastic Ground Motions and Incremental Dynamic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: This paper critically evaluates the probabilistic seismic performance of existing buildings. During the process, the non-stationary stochastic ground motions and incremental dynamic analysis (IDA) are adopted. The principles of non-stationary stochastic ground motions are introduced, and the structural performance under the earthquake excitations is evaluated. The paper lays the foundation for the further performance assessment of infrastructures considering the stochastic characteristics of earthquakes in the future.

articleTitle: Unmanned-System-Based Solution for Coastal Submerged Outfall Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Land-based sewage discharge is closely related to the marine environment, and it is necessary to monitor, evaluate, and regulate this discharge in a scientific and comprehensive manner. However, it is often difficult to effectively detect and monitor the large number and concealment of submerged coastal outfalls. To address this challenge, we present an unmanned system submerged outfall detection method utilizing an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) thermal infrared sensor and an unmanned surface vehicle (USV) side-scan sonar operating in concert. Taking a typical coastal area of Shanghai submerged outfall detection as an example, the unmanned system detection methods identified 51 suspected submerged outfalls in a shoreline survey area of approximately 35.5 km, of which 49 were reviewed and confirmed to exist, with a survey success rate of 96.1%. Specifically, 18 newly discovered submerged outfalls and 31 known submerged outfalls were also identified, i.e., the success rate for the registered submerged outfalls reached 100%. The data not only verified the effectiveness and reliability of the detection method, but also provided essential data for transparent and standardized sewage discharge, scientific and accurate sewage treatment, and protection of the water quality and biodiversity in coastal areas.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of deep foundation pit excavation based on Moore-Coulomb
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to study the influence of Moore-Coulomb model and its parameters on the simulation of deep foundation pit deformation and ensure the safe construction of foundation pit in the construction process, the finite element analysis method is used to analyze the change of Moore-Coulomb model in the simulation of deep foundation pit in the excavation process. By comparing and analyzing the actual monitoring results, the applicability of Moore-Coulomb model to simulate the deformation of deep foundation pit is obtained. The results show that in the prediction of ground settlement, settlement displacement of surrounding buildings, horizontal displacement and vertical displacement of piles, there is little difference between the predicted value of Moore-Coulomb model and the actual monitoring value, and the variation trend of each project simulation value of Moore-Coulomb model under different reference stress is the same as the actual monitoring value. The research conclusion reveals that the Moore-Coulomb constitutive model under different reference stress has certain reference value for the prediction of deep foundation pit excavation deformation.

articleTitle: Short-term water level prediction of Hongze Lake by Prophet-LSTM combined model based on LAE
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Aiming at the accuracy of short-term water level forecasting, a combination model short-term water level forecasting method based on Prophet model and long short-term memory network (LSTM) is proposed. Firstly, the Prophet prediction model and the LSTM prediction model are established respectively, and then based on the least absolute error (LAE), the two methods are combined with different weights to obtain a new combination model. The water level data of Hongze Lake is used as an example to verify. The experimental results show that the proposed model solves the problem that the prophet model cannot mine the nonlinear features in the data and the LSTM model is insufficient in predicting the periodic changes of the data. Compared with the above two models, the proposed model has better prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the particle size distribution of on-site rockfill using mask R-CNN deep learning model
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Particle size distribution (PSD) of the on-site rockfill is one of the most critical factors in evaluating the quality assessment of the rock-filled concrete (RFC). Due to the large quantities and volume, it is difficult to measure the grain size of each rock manually. Image-based methods are widely adopted for the grain segmentation, but the result is not ideal if the rocks are closely connected and overlapped. In this study, a new model Mask R-CNN from the perspective of deep learning is deployed to develop an automatic measurement method of rockfill PSD. The model training was conducted using photos captured from on-site rockfill in Fengguang RFC dam of China. The results of the trained model agree well with the artificial measurements, and it proves Mask R-CNN as an effective technology for the automated estimation of the rockfill PSD in the engineering practice.

articleTitle: Meso-parameters Calibration of Rock Specimens Based on Flat-Joint Contact Model
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Based on the design of experiments (DOE) and the response surface method, we studied the mesoscopic parameters calibration for hard rocks in three-dimensional particle flow code (PFC). First, using the range analysis and multivariate analysis of variance, the linear relationship between mesoscopic and macroscopic parameters is established. Then, we used the response surface method to obtain the nonlinear relationship between the mesoscopic parameters and the macroscopic response. Finally, this problem was transformed into a nonlinear multi objective mathematical programming problem, and the genetic algorithm was utilized to solve it. To verify our proposed method, we compared the obtained results with the physical tests. The results show that the error of macroscopic parameters was less than 10%. A computer calibration program interface was developed based on the proposed model. This model and the computer program can be used in the rock calibrations for numerical simulations in the future.

articleTitle: Research on Port truck trajectory completion based on Long Short-Term Memory model and Speed distribution characteristics
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In the process of port intelligent transformation, real-time completion of missing truck trajectory data plays a vital role in the qualitative data collection of port production operations and the establishment of port digital twin systems. Focusing on the port-specific scenario, this article introduces a method of completing the trajectory of the truck based on the long short-term memory (LSTM), followed by empirical data analysis method. The neural network was deployed to train and predict the trajectory data of trucks in the port. At the same time, it explores the possibility that making a rough prediction of the long-term missing data by considering the historical data and analyzing the truck’s speed distribution characteristics. Compared with previous studies, the method proposed in this paper provides new ideas and methods for collecting missing trajectories of trucks in ports.

articleTitle: Secondary Development and Application of Revit Based on Information Management and Interaction
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The application of BIM Technology in architectural engineering design is developed based on the data interaction function. After analyzing and studying the existing building models, it is found that there are still large functional requirements and exploitable space in the information management and data interaction functions. Through the secondary development of Revit, the information management and data interaction functions can be effectively optimized, Greatly improve work efficiency. This paper briefly expounds the principle of the Revit secondary development, and briefly describes the design basis of information management and data interaction function. Further, the secondary development of element acquisition based on the Revit API and the application of element filter are carried out to achieve the application of filtering data retrieval and processing.

articleTitle: Risk Analysis and Smart Safety Monitoring of Underground Municipal Water Pipe Gallery Project
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The underground municipal water pipeline gallery project is a water conservancy engineering, with high risk, which makes important contributions to urban industrial and civil water use. Based on the 4M principle (Man/ Machine/ Mecdium/ Management) of accident prevention, this paper uses the systematic risk management theory method to identify and classify the risks of underground water pipeline gallery engineering from “Point-Line-Area-Volume”. The results show that the risk factors in the tunneling area are accounted for the largest proportion. The highest risk factors appear in job positions. Based on the Internet of Things technology, cloud computing technology and wireless transmission technology, this paper proposes a new smart water conservancy system to monitor the risk factors. It is described for illustrating the architecture and functional modules. In addition, it is investigated about the application of these smart monitoring methods in actual projects. The results imply that the efficiency of intelligent safety monitoring methods is more than 7 times that of personnel inspections. The research conclusions can provide references for the implementation of risk identification and smart monitoring of underground municipal water pipeline gallery projects, and further improve the level of project safety management and disaster control.

articleTitle: Application of D-InSAR Technology in Monitoring Land-surface Subsidence After an Earthquake
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: With the advantages of all-weather, all-day, large-scale, high-precision, and dynamic-continuity, D-InSAR technology has become a new tool with development potential in the field of surface deformation monitoring and has played an important role in disaster prevention and mitigation. In this paper, the SAR data before and after a 6.7-magnitude earthquake in Kaohsiung of Taiwan, China on February 6, 2016 have been processed by differential interference using the two-track method to obtain the surface deformation before and after the earthquake, and the research results demonstrate that the maximum surface uplift caused by the Kaohsiung earthquake in Taiwan is up to 16 cm and the maximum surface subsidence is up to 12.5 cm, which realizes the monitoring of surface subsidence after the disaster and provides important basic information for disaster prevention and mitigation.

articleTitle: Study on Water Balance and Variations in Water Level of Daihai Lake
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Daihai Lake is the third largest inland lake and an important wetland nature reserve in Inner Mongolia, which plays an important role in the plateau ecosystem. This paper analyzes the interannual water level of Daihai Lake from 1960 to 2019 and the characteristics of interannual water level variation from 2010 to 2019 in response to its severe situation of continuous decline in water level. And through the water balance model, this paper focuses on the change of lake inflows and outflows from 2010 to 2019, and determines the average multi-year water shortage in Daihai Lake. The results show that the historical water level of Daihai Lake showed a downward trend from 1960 to 2019, and the shrinking ratio reached 62%. In recent five years (2015 to 2019), the shrinking rate was the largest (the decline rate of water level: -0.43m/a; lake shrinking rate: -2.27km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/a). From 2010 to 2010, the average water shortage was 25.6779 million m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The research results can provide a scientific theoretical basis for the sustainable development of Daihai Lake.

articleTitle: Gross Error Identification of Reservoir and Dam Safety Monitoring Data Based on Outlier Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Based on safety monitoring results to evaluate the overall safety and stability of reservoirs and dams, meanwhile to analyze the reason of abnormal condition and take corresponding measures when necessary, all of those are important means to ensure reservoirs and dams safety from accidents. At present, reservoir and dam safety monitoring is developing towards online monitoring. In order to improve the accuracy and timeliness of analysis results, it is necessary to effectively eliminate the gross error from the prototype monitoring data. Based on the outlier characteristics of gross error, this paper processed a new “group” by using effect variable value and its measured interval, so that the corresponding relationship between the real gross error in the original data and the outlier value in the new “group” could be established, and then the gross error was identified in combination with outlier reasons. The case analysis verifies that this approach is capable of identifying gross error outstandingly.

articleTitle: Numerical Study on Performance of Vortex Settling Basin with a Perforated Deflector
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Perforating the deflector of a vortex settling basin (VSB) has been proposed as a retrofit to prevent the VSB failure that is caused by excessive sediment deposition on the deflector. In this study, numerical simulations were conducted using ANSYS Fluent to investigate the internal flow patterns of the VSBs with the deflector perforated in two different ways, one perforated outside the overflow region only and the other perforated entirely. The trajectories of sediment particles and the sediment removal efficiencies of the VSBs were also simulated and analyzed based on their internal flow features. The VSB with the partially-perforated deflector exhibited a stronger vortex flow and a larger flow velocity above the deflector compared to that with the entirely-perforated deflector. It performed a high sediment removal efficiency close to the original VSB design and also a significant reduction of sediment deposition on the deflector. For the VSB with the entirely-perforated deflector, the sediment removal efficiency was much lower, while the sediment deposition was not reduced as effectively.

articleTitle: Study on Design and Construction Safety of Open-cut Structure of Railway Tunnels in Shallow Water-bearing Soft Soils
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In the water-rich complex soft soil stratum, there are great difficulties in manual-excavated pile construction in cutting engineering, and it is very difficult to dig for forming piles in the water-rich sand stratum. There is water seepage and sand gushing, which leads to the risk of deformation and hole collapse, and the construction risk is extremely high. Based on the engineering example of changing the cutting of the portal section of the New Changqiangling Tunnel into an open cut tunnel during the construction of the second line of the Yangpingguan–Ankang Railway, and the stratum conditions and groundwater conditions revealed on-site, the paper introduces in detail the design and construction of cast-in-situ bored pile retaining open-cut structure which is used under the condition that the original design of cutting pile-sheet wall structure is difficult to be implemented, and it makes a detailed analysis of the advantages and disadvantages of cast-in-situ bored pile retaining open-cut structure with respect of structural safety, construction safety risk, construction quality control, construction cost, construction period, and operation and maintenance. The paper provides a very valuable reference for similar engineering design in the future as it solves the problem of the construction of deep cutting or shallow-buried tunnels in shallow-buried soils under site-controlled conditions, and at the same time greatly reduces the operation safety risk of the railway in deep cuttings.

articleTitle: An Integrated Space-air-ground Monitoring and Early Warning System of Landslide Disaster
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated disaster monitoring and early warning system based on multiple technical means of space, air, and ground. Aiming at the pilot area of geological disaster monitoring, various technical means of space, air and earth are comprehensively applied to monitor geological disaster points. The spaceborne InSAR technology and optical remote sensing interpretation technology are used to conduct a large-scale early census of the test area. Then, lidar technology and UAV photogrammetry technology are used to regularly monitor local geological disaster communities, and the ground monitoring equipment arranged at the disaster points is used for remote continuous observation to realize real-time monitoring and real-time early warning. Finally, an integrated monitoring and early warning system is built.

articleTitle: Preparation and properties of bendable concrete for bridge-deck link slabs
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: To obtain ultra-high-strength bendable concrete, herein, ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene (PE), polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), and copper-plated microsteel fibers are used as reinforcement to prepare four groups of bendable concrete. The compressive strength, bending strength, and bending toughness of the obtained concrete are evaluated. The results show that the fibers improve the compressive strength and bendable strength of the concrete, and the reinforcement effect differentiates from the fiber type. PE fibers show the most significant effect on the toughness of the concrete, followed by PE–PVA hybrid and PVA fibers, and that of steel fibers is the worst.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of seabed suspended span pipeline under wave action
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Under the self-weight, the internal fluid weight, the external environment, the submarine pipeline has the potential to be damaged. Aimed at the stability of submarine pipeline accident, the submarine hydrological and geological conditions are analyzed, by numerical simulation method, the characteristics of unburied pipeline without considering internal water pressure of the pipe and under wave loading are analyzed. According to the DNV specification, the maximum allowable span length of the submarine pipeline is determined from the equivalent stress of the pipeline, which is not more than the allowable stress of the material, and the safety evaluation of the submarine pipeline is carried out. The research results have certain reference value and practical significance in guiding the design and construction of pipeline

articleTitle: Study on reciprocal relationship among water amount-water quality-water efficiency based on the SWAT_WAQER model : —A case study of the Yulin catchment
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to quantitatively analyze the interrelationship among total water consumption, water use efficiency and river water quality, this paper takes the Yulin Basin as the study object and constructs a “quantity-quality-efficiency” joint regulation model based on SWAT_WAQER, and calibrates runoff and water quality. By setting five scenarios of industrial water use efficiency and agricultural irrigation water use efficiency, the SWAT_WAQER model is used to simulate and analyze the total water consumption, pollution emission, and response state of water quality of river cross-sections under each scenario, and to analyze the interaction among them. The results show that the SWAT_WAQER model constructed in this paper performs well and it is applicable for changes in national economy water consumption, pollutants discharged into rivers and river water quality concentration under different water conservation scenarios. In the Yulin Basin, water consumption of per CNY 10,000 of industrial added value, industrial water consumption and river water quality up-to-standard rate show a linkage relationship of simultaneous decrease and simultaneous increase; water efficiency of irrigation, irrigation water use and water quality up-to-standard rate show a linkage relationship of “as one falls, another rises”; changes in water consumption of per CNY 10,000 of industrial added value have obvious influence on river water quality concentration, but changes in water efficiency of irrigation have limited influence on river water quality concentration.

articleTitle: Seismic Performance Analysis and Safety Assessment of Wind Turbine Tower System
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The seismic safety and serviceability of main wind turbine tower system structures after an earthquake is important to the seismic reliability of the whole wind engineering. This study proposed a performance-based seismic design methodology for wind towers system based on the incremental dynamic analysis (IDA) by finite element method, which taken into account the interaction of the tower system with the soil ground. An IDA-based seismic assessment method including fractile and fragility analyses for a 1.5MW wind turbine tower system case was developed. Then, the occurrence and development of the concrete foundation cracks, failure modes and mechanisms were investigated according to a series of nonlinear numerical simulation tests.

articleTitle: Effect of Admixture Content on The Strength of Plant Concrete
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Strength, porosity, and pH are the three vital parameters of planting concrete. The traditional planting concrete is mainly made of cement and coarse aggregate. Generally, the pH value of concrete is relatively high, which makes it difficult to meet plant production needs. In order to reduce the pH of concrete, admixtures such as silica fume, mineral powder, and fly ash are often added when preparing planting concrete. Unfortunately, although admixtures can effectively improve various indicators of concrete, they also have an impact on the strength of concrete. In this paper, the effect of different amount of mineral powder and carbon powder on the strength of planting concrete is studied through experiments, which provides a reference for the preparation of planted concrete.

articleTitle: The reconstruction of lake water levels with a deep belief network based method considering the spatial and temporal heterogeneity in contributions of the driving factors
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Satellite altimetry plays a significant role in monitoring the dynamic changes of inland lake water levels (WLs). However, the altimeter data are generally temporally discontinuous, due to the influence of track distance, temporal internal, and quality problems. In this paper, we proposed a deep belief network (DBN) based method for the reconstruction of lake WLs, to fill in the temporal gaps in the sequence of altimetry-derived WLs. This was achieved by learning the relationships between WLs and the related auxiliary environmental data. Partial least squares regression (PLSR) algorithm was used to select the most correlated input variables considering the spatial and temporal heterogeneity in contributions of the driving factors. Two typical lakes in Chinese Altai region, i.e., Ulungu and Jili, were chosen as the study area, and their continuous monthly WL datasets from 2003 to 2018 were reconstructed. The evaluation results show that introducing variable selection can significantly improve the performance of deep learning models. The reconstructed WL datasets have the potential to be used in monitoring fine-scale changes of lake WLs.

articleTitle: Time-variant seismic reliability analysis of slopes with combined uncertainties based on probability density evolution method
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Time-variant reliability are gaining much more popularity in geotechnical engineering due to the fact that the internal geotechnical parameters are change with the time and the external environmental excitation are random processes, which is of great significance in the service-life assessment, resilience-based assessment and intelligent disaster reduction. Considering that most existing studies of time-variant reliability analysis of slopes concentrated on the static conditions, which have neglected the time-varying behaviour of intensity and frequency of input seismic loading, the present study proposed an efficient probabilistic method for the time-variant reliability analysis of slope under the seismic loading, in which the combined uncertainties of spatially variable soil properties and the randomness of seismic loading are simultaneously considered. The time-dependent behaviour of seismic performance of slope under the no-stationary stochastic processes of seismic loading is revealed. The time-variant seismic reliability results and the probability density function of dynamic failure time are calculated by the proposed method. The results from the various intensities of input seismic loading, seismic performance criteria, seismic performance indexes and uncertainties are also compared in our study to illustrate the effect of different factors on the time-variant seismic reliability of slopes.

articleTitle: Numerical study on seismic performance of concrete filled steel tube column base with high strength reinforcing bars
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: This paper carries out a numerical study on the seismic performance of innovative concrete filled steel tube (CFST) column base with high strength reinforcing bars. Based on the experiments of the proposed CFST column base, the FEM analysis model is developed using the ABAQUS software. In the analysis model, the corresponding material constitutive relationships, the meshing method, the interaction, and the boundary condition are determined for the innovative CFST column bases. Analysis results are in good agreement with the test results. The tensile and compressive region of the steel tube and the base plate are all yielded. The base plate is in a bending status and an interspace appears from the foundation which matches the test phenomenon well. In the design practice, the parameter matching needs to be considered the proposed column base.

articleTitle: Analysis of influence of material parameter randomness on temperature control of concrete gravity dam during construction
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Temperature load is counted as one of the main causes of cracks in mass concrete during construction. The current temperature control simulation analysis is based on determined parameters to evaluate the risk of concrete cracking. The tensile strength adopted derives from test data, and the tensile stress is calculated through concrete test or finite element simulation, without considering the randomness of the parameters. In this paper, the variability of mechanical and thermal properties of concrete gravity dam is considered, and the influence of the variability of material parameters of mass concrete and the uncertainty of their development with concrete age on the temperature control of concrete gravity dam is studied via whole-process simulation calculation of the whole dam, so as to provide reference for the crack prevention of mass concrete during construction.

Author Keywords: Whole-process analysis of the whole dam

articleTitle: Research on the application of BIM-based digital bridge design, construction and operation and maintenance secondary development
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: At present, digital development in bridge engineering still has a significant shortage, and the information level of existing bridge projects is relatively low. Therefore, this paper presents a conceptual model to enhance the integration of bridge digital design, construction, operation and maintenance (O&M) based on Building Information Modelling (BIM) for the secondary development of bridge life cycle construction. This paper first proposes the conceptual construction of an integrated platform for intelligent bridge construction to realize the sharing of data and integration of modules in all phases of design, construction, and O&M to improve the efficiency of collaborative management of intelligent systems bridges. Secondly, the platform builds a data-sharing center based on BIM-based technologies such as componentization, informatization, and number-model separation to realize the cascading and interaction of data in each stage, which solves the problem of information transfer omission and difficulty in sharing in different stages of bridge engineering design, construction, and O&M management. Finally, a data collection and integration platform is built using the advantages of 3D visualization and efficient collaboration of BIM technology. The application of intelligent information technology in bridge construction is studied to improve information application and management of intelligent bridge design, construction, O&M.

articleTitle: Inland River Simulation of Coastal Cities Based on Real-time Control (RTC) Rules
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Urban rivers are important landscape and environmental carriers of cities. Aiming at the ecological regulation of inland river water level under the action of tide in coastal cities, an application case of RTC and hydrodynamic model in Baima River Basin in Fuzhou is presented. The results show that the model is accurate and reliable. The constructed RTC rules can automatically regulate the gate according to the water level in the simulation process, and achieve the expectation. The practical application of RTC rules is discussed, and the future development is prospected.

articleTitle: A long term cost effective slop safety monitoring using emergency activated Brillouin optic fiber sensors
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: This paper designed a long term cost effective slop safety monitoring strategy using emergency activated embedded Brillouin optic fiber sensors. Reinforced optic fibers were installed along the longitudinal steel bars of the anti-slide piles at construction stage and permanently integrated into piles with concrete placement. To reduce life cycle maintenance cost, no monitoring center or data acquisition devices were installed on site, only a mobile DPP-BOTDA high spatial resolution interrogator was prepared. The embedded optical fibers were firstly measured with initial strain values after pile construction was completed and turned into standby mode in normal service condition. When abnormal circumstances occur, the embedded optical fibers would be activated and measured again to conduct safety assessment. A successful demonstration of this strategy is reported.

articleTitle: Research on the performance of base asphalt mixture for application in pouring semi flexible pavement
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Based on the asphalt mixture gradation volume design method and successful design gradation range applied in the previous testing road, three kinds of composite gradation passing rates were designed for comparative research. In this work, we taking the pouring semi-flexible pavement base asphalt mixture sfac20 as an example. According to different single-side compaction tests, including 50 times, 75 times, 100 times and 125 times, the standard Marshall specimens were prepared. The experimental parameters of the best compaction times and the best composite gradation were also investigated Polyester fiber and high viscosity agent, were selected as two additives. When the admixture amount was 3%, the admixture method was single admixture or compound admixture. The performance of the mixture was evaluated by comprehensive indexes such as Marshall stability, flow value, porosity, Cantabro Test, Schellenberg Binder Drainage Test, asphalt mixture uniaxial penetration test and grouting rate. With the increase of compaction times, the mixture tests of the three gradation types showed the same change trend. The best results were obtained when the single side compaction was 75 times. When the number of compaction exceeds 75 times, the embedded structure of the mixture was easy to be broken. When polyester fiber was mixed with high viscosity and the dosage was both 0.3%, the indexes of the mixture exhibited better performance compared with other control groups, especially the results of Cantabro Test. The test results are expected to provide a reference for the design of matrix asphalt mixture of cast-in-place semi-flexible pavement and promote the better engineering application of semi flexible pavement.

articleTitle: Abnormality Behavior Recognition Method for Ship in Bridge Waters Considering Small-Sample Problem
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: With the development of transportation, more and more bridges are built, and the safety of bridges is becoming more and more important. In the waters of the bridge area, more and more ships pass through, and the navigation environment is more complex than that of the ordinary channel. For the staff of the traffic management department and bridge maintenance, it is necessary to always pay attention to the behavior of passing ships and remind the ships with abnormal behavior to prevent accidents that damage the bridge. Firstly, by analyzing the collision risk of ship bridge and the abnormal behavior of ship itself, this paper combines the two to obtain the judgment standard of ship abnormal behavior in the waters of bridge area; then, considering the small sample problem of ship abnormal behavior in the actual data, a large number of ship trajectory data are generated by the method of ship motion equation and random data generation. Based on the generated ship trajectory data, the identification model of ship abnormal behavior in the bridge area is established by using BP neural network classification method to give early warning of ship abnormal behavior, Provide technical means for the safe passage of ships in the waters of the bridge area to reduce or avoid the losses caused to the bridge.

articleTitle: Evaluation on Operation Performance Improvement of RCC Dam using Cloud Model
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The objective function of economic benefit evaluation of engineering reinforcement is established for the improvement of operation performance of roller compacted concrete (RCC) dam, through maximizing the comprehensive benefit, minimizing the repair cost and the risk degree. Based on the cloud model theory, an innovative optimal decision-making model is proposed. These methods were applied in a RCC dam under operation for nearly 20 years, the variation laws of deformation, stress and seepage under different reinforcement schemes were explored through numerical simulation, and the evaluation indexes were scored by experts. The calculation results of the cloud model comprehensive evaluation set for different schemes are obtained, and the implementation effect of each scheme is evaluated accordingly.

articleTitle: Research on the Best Route Strategy Model of Rescue Patrol Based on Floyd Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The best route strategy is actually graph theory, and its core is the shortest path problem. Floyd algorithm is the classic algorithm for finding the shortest path. It has the advantages of simple, effective, compact structure, high planning efficiency, and is widely used. In this paper, a practical rescue patrol case is presented. The best rescue route is discussed from two cases, which are all known and partially known, and the Floyd algorithm is used to build the model to solve the problem. Finally, the corresponding best rescue route strategy is given. The results show that the best route strategy model of rescue patrol based on Floyd algorithm solves the practical problems and is an effective shortest path algorithm. At the same time, case analysis also provides theoretical reference and reference for fire safety relief, intelligent disaster prevention and mitigation, marine biological engineering and other fields, and has wide application value.

articleTitle: Low temperature load limitation of long Span Concrete truss composite arch Bridge
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to study the load limiting method of long-span concrete truss composite arch bridge at low temperature, the finite element analysis of the operating force of a 138m truss composite arch bridge at low temperature was firstly carried out, including the deflection change and stress distribution caused by temperature. Secondly, the load characteristics of trucks on the bridge are analyzed and the lower limit load is analyzed based on WIM data. Finally, the analysis results show that the long-term deformation of the truss composite arch bridge under the action of temperature is m-shaped, and the structure has a large tensile stress at the junction of empty and solid sides in the middle of span and at the lower chord position at the double columns. This kind of bridge is very sensitive to the effect of temperature. The influence of vehicle load on the structure under low temperature should be paid attention to and the relevant load limiting method is proposed to provide reference for this kind of bridge.

articleTitle: TCN water level prediction based on feature decomposition and reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low water level prediction accuracy caused by the temporal and spatial heterogeneity and nonlinear characteristics of Hongze Lake, a TCN water level prediction model based on feature decomposition and reconstruction is proposed. The data breakpoints are locally predicted and completed by ARIMA; the data is decomposed based on CEEMDAN, and the characteristics of different frequencies are extracted; the multi-component TCN prediction model is established, and each component is reconstructed to obtain the final water level prediction result. Experiments show that compared with the four models of TCN, LSTM, EMD-TCN, and CEEMDAN-LSTM, the performance of this model is improved; in the Hongze Lake water level prediction, the MAE is only 0.027 meters, and the RMSE is only 0.040 meters. The prediction accuracy Reaching 99.4%, it has higher engineering practical value.

articleTitle: Application of Computer Vision on Displacement Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Monitoring accuracy and verifiability of displacement of structure is essential for project’s safety. This paper presents a kind of design method of displacement monitoring system based on computer vision, including scale acquisition module, visual recognition module and wireless communication network. Also taking static level as example to demonstrate the key points and realization methods of designing each module, an approach to recognize the scale value from picture is proposed based on the invariance of imaging range, along with optimized methods of improving picture’s pixel and intercepting specified match region to enhance accuracy of visual recognition module’s output. Test result shows the system is capable of monitoring displacement automatically at low cost, the optimized methods could upgrade accuracy, recognition precision achieves 0.16mm, meanwhile, the visualization feature of system can be assistant method of manual monitoring to ensure the verifiability of data.

articleTitle: Durability analysis and prediction of reinforced concrete structures in coastal areas
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The durability of reinforced concrete structures corroded by chloride ions in the marine environment is an urgent problem to be solved. In this paper, the corrosion behavior of chloride ion on reinforced concrete structure is investigated. Based on the existing test results and chloride ion transmission model, the influence of sea sand on the durability of concrete structure is considered. The chloride ion intrusion model and the calculation method of initial corrosion time of reinforcement are introduced, and a case study is carried out in order to provide support for predicting the service life of concrete structure.

articleTitle: Simulation of Precipitation in 50 Gamma World Cities for the 20th Century Using Random Walk
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Unforeseeably large or small precipitations can lead to huge damages in given area. Mathematical description of precipitation is an important step to understand the precipitation patterns, and paves the way to possibly predict the precipitation with models. In this study, we attempt to use the random walk model to simulate the annual precipitation in 50 gamma world cities for the 20<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> century. The results show that the random walk model can accomplish simulations, suggesting the random walk model can describe the precipitation in these cities.

articleTitle: Large-eddy Simulation of Turbulent Flow in A Vertical Slot Fishway
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In this study, Large-Eddy Simulation (LES) is carried out to investigate turbulent flow through a typical vertical slot fishway (VSF), in which extensive field measurements have been taken with a 3D Micro-Acoustic Doppler Velocimeter (ADV). The computational domain is idealized as a box including two pairs of baffles and the periodic boundary condition is applied streamwisely to achieve fully-develop state. The calculated time-averaged velocity profiles are in good agreement with the ADV measurements, as well as the turbulent kinetic energy distribution. Furthermore, 2D turbulence distribution is presented by contours of vertical vorticity in horizontal planes to highlight the K-H instability, while 3D turbulence structures are visualized with iso-surfaces of the Q-criterion to track vortex production, propagation and dissipation.

articleTitle: Experimental study on ship’s mooring force of arched longitudinal beam wharf
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: A new type of wharf structure with arched longitudinal beams has been proposed to adapt to open sea deep water area. This study focuses on the experiment of ship’s mooring force, which is important in reasonable design and safety operation. In the experiment, by changing the water depth, wave period, wave height and different vessels’ tonnages, mooring forces and impact forces are obtained. The results show that mooring force and impact force are both proportional to wave period and wave height, and the influence of wave height on the load is larger than that of wave period. In the three translational degrees of freedom, sway is most affected by wave, and heave impact is relatively minor. The present results will provide guidelines in the design and construction of the deep water wharf.

articleTitle: Analysis of Road Performance of Modified Asphalt Mixture of Waste Cigarette Butts Based on Grey Correlation Method
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The waste cigarette butts were added to the asphalt mix as modifier and the ratio design was carried out. The high temperature stability, water stability and water permeability were studied and analyzed by Wheel rutting test, Immersed Marshall test and Infiltration test respectively. It was found that the road performance of the waste cigarette butt modified asphalt mixture was better than that of the normal asphalt mixture. Finally, Grey correlation analysis was used to rank the importance of the main influencing factors (asphalt dosage, temperature and soot dosing) on the road worthiness of the waste soot modified asphalt mixes, which provides a reliable basis for the testing and design of waste soot modified asphalt mixes and is conducive to improving the road worthiness of waste soot mixes.

articleTitle: Study on Seepage Monitoring and Analysis of SL Gravity Dam
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The research shows that the accidents caused by seepage damage account for more than 20% of all the accidents of concrete gravity dams. The seepage safety state of concrete gravity dams has a great influence on the safety of concrete gravity dam. Therefore, it is very important to monitor and analyze the seepage safety of concrete gravity dams. After the completion of SL hydraulic project, the seepage of gravity dam body and foundation as well as the left and right banks is monitored and analyzed. The monitoring items include seepage flow of key parts, seepage pressure gauge and seepage around the dam. According to the analysis, the safety condition of normal operation of the dam can be checked and judged. It can help us test and judge the safety status of normal operation of the dam. The analysis results show that the anti-seepage system works normally at the dam and foundation, and the seepage flow tends to be stable, which conforms to the actual seepage law. The seepage monitoring design of SL dam is reasonable and can fully reflect the seepage situation at different parts of the dam.

articleTitle: Application of Flow Field Analysis in the Design of Artificial Lakes: A Case Study of Urban Lake in Linzhang County
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Different from natural lakes, atificial lakes usually pay more attention to their landscape ecological functions than to their hydrological characteristics in the process of their design. The method of flow field simulation can be used to analyze the changes in hydrological characteristics of artificial lakes arising from the influence of morphological characteristics, so as to provide support for the optimization and adjustment of lake morphology to improve the dynamic conditions of artificial lakes and maintain their water quality. With the artificial lakes in the urban area of Linzhang County as an example, MIKE21 model was used to simulate the flow field of the preliminary lake morphology, and then to verify and analyze the adjusted lake morphology. Based on the simulation results of the flow field and the surrounding land use types, the construction scheme of the artificial lake revetment was proposed to provide a scientific basis for the design of the artificial lakes.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of waterway facilities management database based on GIS
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Aiming at the current status of waterway facility management with the low degree of information, a section of the Sunan Canal was taken as the research object, the idea of constructing a GIS-based canal waterway facility management database was proposed. The facilities were converted into vector graphics according to geometric characteristics and classified according to types. The spatial distribution of facilities was expressed by superimposing thematic layers. The attribute structure was used for storing information related to the waterway. In order to ensure the accuracy of data transfer, the waterway element coding should be designed in a standardized way, the multimedia data should be linked to reduce the response time of the database, and the topological relation should be used to control the quality of spatial data. By constructing a waterway facility management database, not only the integration of waterway information and two-way query of information are realized, but also spatial information measurement, data statistical analysis and thematic map production can be carried out. The database is taken as an example to provide a reference for waterway information management.

articleTitle: Research on Ecological Protection of Side Slope along Railway Subgrade Based on BIM+GIS
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Soil erosion is a common cause of damage to railway subgrades. However, at this stage, roadbed protection only considers the treatment of both sides of the subgrades, and little consideration is given to the source of the subgrade scouring area. In this paper, the loess area with poor stability is used as the research terrain. With the help of GIS, the spatial overlay analysis of the study area is carried out to accurately identify the different soil erosion intensities of the base design area, thereby solving the problems of source protection and accurate layout. On this basis, a slope ecological protection system based on BIM technology was constructed, and then through the GIS system, a solution was proposed for the fusion of the two data and the generation of composite DEM, and the secondary soil and water analysis was completed based on the composite DEM.

articleTitle: Study on Flood Control Optimal Operation of Reservoir Group-Taking Pihe River Basin as an Example
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: With the change of climatic conditions and the flood control situation of river basin, the present status of flood control project and the original design conditions have changed to some degree with major changes in the flood control conditions of river basin. And the joint flood control operation of reservoir group has become the trend of flood control in the river basin. As regards the frequent flood disaster in the river basin and the business demand of flood disaster prevention in the basin of Pihe River, a tributary of Huai River, the study on flood control joint operation of reservoir group has been made based on flood control tasks undertaken by four mixed multi-reservoirs in Foziling, Mozitan, Bailianya and Xianghongdian. Through flood control optimal operation, the flood control risk has been greatly reduced, which bolsters the flood control safety in the Pihe River basin.

articleTitle: On-site experiment methods on the compaction detection of rock-filled concrete
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The compaction of SCC filling the voids of rockfill is greatly significant to guarantee the safety for rock-filled concrete dams in practical engineering. Most of the on-site experiment methods, such as drilling core samples, infrared in-hole TV, focus on the compactness detection of the hardened RFC. In this paper, some exploratory methods of on-site experiment are conducted for the compactness detection of fresh SCC filling. The monitoring instruments are prearranged to be embedded in different spatial structures of the rock-fill voids in the storehouses of RFC. The experiment results manifest that: (1) Wired bulbs with sensing electrodes (WBSE) can detect the filling compactness of fresh SCC by alarm light; (2) The self-compacting concrete can mostly fill in the voids, while the compacting effect will be poor at the fragmentary voids with many small rocks (less than 300mm), and it is worst at the throat void. The actual filling state is important for engineers to evaluate the construction quality of RFC dams.

articleTitle: Research on restoration and landscape remodeling of mining wasteland based on Brandi’s theory of restoration
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: With the development of economic, the reconstruction of mining wasteland is more important. For restoration and landscape remodeling of mining wasteland, the Brandi s theory of restoration can greatly improve the appearance of environment, form a systematic landscape pattern, and stimulate the humanistic and economic values as ecological heritage. Taking the Banan mining site in Chongqing as an example, the concept of restoration of geological heritage is developed, the multiple meanings and values are extended. The results can make enhancement of the land ecological economy value, also can promote regional ecosystem stability and sustainable development of local economy.

articleTitle: Study on Arrangement of Advance Heading for Extra-long Double-barrel Single-track Tunnel
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The position of advance heading directly affects the difficulty of opening cross adits, the degree of secondary disturbance to the rocks caused by drilling and blasting, and the volume of construction ventilation and drainage. In this paper, the construction plan of "advance heading (for later enlargement)" of the extra-long double-barrel single-track tunnel is taken as the background, and the position of advance heading and the effect of controlling rock deformation by heading is emphatically studied. According to the study results, it is suggested that the heading should be located at the middle lower section of the tunnel. First, it is beneficial to set up the cross adits to assist the tunnel excavation for Track I. Second, it can be used as the construction drainage and ventilation channel to reduce the length of the counter-slope drainage section and lower the ventilation and drainage volumes during construction. At the same time, advance heading has unloading effect, and the effect of controlling the rock deformation of the tunnel is remarkable.

articleTitle: Research on excavation supporting measures for the dome of giant cylindrical surge chamber
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The excavation and support of large underground caverns in a complex geological environment have brought great challenges to engineering design. The tailwater surge chamber of Baihetan Hydropower Station is a huge project with a maximum excavation diameter of 48 m. Geological factors including high stress, interlayer dislocation zone, and columnar joints impact the cavern's stability, making construction difficult. To investigate the cylindrical surge chamber dome's excavation and support technologies, as well as the stability of the surrounding rock, multiple methods have been applied, including empirical analogy, numerical calculation and field investigation. An excavation and support scheme of “high layered partition, horizontal sector partition, top-down, from inside to outside, area by area excavation and layer by layer support” has been proposed. The anchor observation tunnel in the shape of a “Wang” was innovatively designed. By presetting the new supporting structure of the anti-hanging dome through the anchor cable, the advanced implementation and monitoring of the support of the huge dome system have been accomplished. The research results are helpful to guide and optimize the subsequent excavation and support design of the cavern construction.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Treatment Technology for Permafrost Soil Foundation in Mohe Airport
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: This article systematically summarizes the treatment plan of permafrost soil foundation during the construction of Mohe Airport, analyzes the changes in ground temperature and settlement during the construction period and operation period, and discusses the feasibility of replacing permafrost soil with non-frost heaving materials. The foundation treatment plan provides effective ideas for airport built in permafrost area.

articleTitle: Effect of sodium hydroxide concentration on the performance of alkali-activated recycled cement-based materials
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Compared with traditional cement, alkai-activated cementitious materials have higher strength, lower hydration heat, simple manufacturing process and less investment. At the same time, this paper uses recyced cement-based materials, the combination of the two groups also conforms to the principle of green, low energy consumption. In this paper, sodium hydroxide was used as alkali excitation reagent to study the macroscopic compressive strength of samples under different concentrations of sodium hydroxide and the influence of calcium carbonate content on macroscopic strength at microscopic scale.

Author Keywords: sodium hydroxide compressive strength micro-scale calcium carbonate

articleTitle: Research on the Mechanical Characteristics of High-Filled Balanced Retaining Wall—Taking a Retaining Wall Project in Mianyang as an Example
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: As a special form of gravity retaining walls, counterweight retaining walls are mostly used to ensure the stability of fill slopes. The D24-D30 section of a retaining wall project in Mianyang is mainly used to support artificial fill slopes with a height of about 10m in the site. It is proposed to consider the use of counterweight retaining wall support for such large fill slopes. Based on this project, this paper derives the calculation formula of earth pressure, which shows that the height of the upper wall is positively correlated with the earth pressure value of the upper wall, and negatively correlated with the earth pressure value of the lower wall; the unloading capacity is getting stronger and stronger, and the position of the counterweight platform has a greater influence on the increase of the earth pressure on the upper wall.

articleTitle: Deformation prediction of gravity dam based on ISADE-OSELM
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Deformation prediction of gravity dams is important measures to ensure dam safety, and is difficult areas of study. In order to better carry out gravity dam safety monitoring, this paper introduced Online Sequential Extreme Learning Machine (OSELM) algorithm to establish gravity dam deformation prediction model. The parameters of OSELM model can be updated by incremental learning, that is different from the traditional batch learning of establish monitor model. The advantage of this learning method is that it helps the model to incorporate the information contained in the latest monitoring data. It optimizes the traditional modeling approach. In addition, the selection method of initial parameters in Self Adaptive Differential Evolution (SADE) is improved, and an Improved Self Adaptive Differential Evolution (ISADE) algorithm is proposed with better global optimization ability. Then it is used to optimize the OSELM model, thus improving the accuracy of OSELM model. In this paper, an example is analyzed by stepwise, ELM, OSELM and ISADE-OSELM models respectively. Generally speaking, the predicted results of ELM and OSELM basically meet the engineering needs. However, the MSE and MAE values of ISADE-OSELM are the smallest, indicating that the accuracy of the model is relatively high, the R2 value of ISADE-OSELM is the largest, indicating that the overall fitting degree of the model is relatively best. That is the comprehensive performance of ISADE-OSELM is relatively optimal. The example analysis shows that the prediction performance of ISADE-OSELM model is improved, and the model can predicte the gravity dam deformation with high accuracy.

Author Keywords: improved Self Adaptive Differential Evolution algorithm

articleTitle: Unused Material Stripping and Capacity Recheck of Shijiagou Stockyard of Jinchuan Hydropower Station based on Geological Three-dimensional Model
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The Shijiagou stockyard is the source of concrete aggregates and rockfill materials for the Jinchuan Hydropower Station. It is extremely important to ensure sufficient stocks in the stockyard. The article uses the self-developed ItasCAD, a geological 3D design platform based on the DSI underlying modeling engine and the “graphics + data” architecture of the Northwestern Institute. Use the 3D digital method to check the capacity of the stockyard, and carry out the geological 3D modeling work based on the preliminary survey data of the Jinchuan Hydropower Station. Establishing stockyard capacity envelope for each excavation elevation model in design slope ratio, in order to achieve the release unwanted material reserves and inquiries. This method can also be used to quickly update the geological model of the stockyard according to the actual geological conditions along with the excavation of the site, combined with the dynamic mining of the stockyard, quickly complete the capacity review work of the stockyard, and realize the dynamic calculation of the stockyard capacity. The results of this research have reference significance and application value for the same type of projects.

articleTitle: Effects of tides and pumping on seawater intrusion in coastal aquifers
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: To study the effect of combined tidal and pumping on seawater intrusion in the coastal aquifer, groundwater flow and salt transport process in the aquifer with and without tidal influence during 365 days of pumping was simulated based on SUTRA. Without tidal influence, the saltwater wedge keeps invading inland with the increase of pumping time. After considering the influence of tides, the discharge from the upper aquifer-sea interface decreases with pumping, and the upper saline plume gradually expands downward, which inhibits further inland intrusion of the saltwater wedge. With the combined effect of tides and pumping, the area of freshwater and saltwater mixing zone increases significantly.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Three Machine Visual Recognition Algorithms in Identification of Un-vibrated Concrete
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Mechanical automatic vibration of concrete is a development direction of civil engineering construction, and automatic vibration accuracy control algorithm is one of the difficulties. This article attempts to use machine vision solutions to solve this problem. Program for three common feature extraction algorithms (Hog algorithm, LBP algorithm, Haar algorithm) is written through Python language. Then the “Support Vector Machine” algorithm is applied to classify the feature data extracted by each algorithm. By this way, the accuracy and efficiency of the three algorithms under different parameters are compared. The test comparison results show that the Hog algorithm is more efficient but the accuracy is average, the LBP algorithm has the highest accuracy but the efficiency is general when multiple training is required, and the Haar algorithm has the relatively lowest accuracy and efficiency. The results can provide a basis for the selection of different algorithms and parameters for various scenarios where the visual inspection and recognition system of un-vibrated concrete may be applied.

articleTitle: Effect of carbon powder content on compressive strength and alkalinity of ecological concrete
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Ecological concrete is characterized by porous and without sand. Plants can grow on the ecological concrete surface and its pores, which is a new choice for revetment engineering. However, the growth of plants always was restricted by the high alkalinity of the ecological concrete. Activated carbon powder was mixed into the ecological concrete to reduce its alkalinity, and the results showed that carbon powder reduced the compressive strength, increased the pH of ecological concrete.

articleTitle: Study on hydraulic characteristics and optimization of the combined weir and hole baffle fishway rest pool
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: According to the fish passage requirements of Cao’e River lock, a three-dimensional turbulent flow model of the fish passage with weir-hole combination bulkhead chamber was established, and the effects of lengthening the resting pool length and adjusting the bulkhead distribution on the resting pool were analyzed in terms of the flow pattern of the chamber, turbulent kinetic energy and the attenuation of the mainstream along the course. The results of the study show that: the three working conditions all have obvious mainstream against the wall phenomenon, two times the length of the fishway resting pool can basically meet the hydraulic requirements of fish on the resting pool, to three times the length of the pool, the resting pool reflux area increases insignificantly; for the straight section of the resting pool chamber, the heterolateral distribution than the same side of the distribution can produce more favorable flow patterns; resting pool length and the same side of the bulkhead heterolateral distribution on the resting pool turbulent kinetic energy effect is small.

articleTitle: Analysis on FRP Strengthening of Cracked Steel Plates Considering Bonding Effect in Cracks
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: When Fiber Reinforced Polymer/Plastic (FRPs) are used to repair cracked steel plates, the bonding materials will be inevitably trapped into cracks. This phenomenon, however, has not been considered in the current theoretical analyses of most scholars. In this paper, a bridging force model was introduced to simulate the bonding materials between upper and lower surfaces of cracks. A finite element model was established for single-surface repairing of cracked steel plates, and the results were compared with the finite element calculation results without considering the bonding effect of binders inside cracks. Besides, the impact of bonding materials inside cracks upon FRP repairing of cracked steel plates was quantified. Results revealed that, in the case of short cracks, the error between two finite element calculations was slight; when the cracks were longer than 40 mm, the difference between calculated stress intensity factors (SIF), crack expansion displacements, and maximum out-of-plane displacements of steel plates were 20.61%, 77.14%, and 35.73% respectively; and the impact of bonding materials in the crack surfaces upon cracked steel plates cannot be ignored.

articleTitle: Research Progress of Self-centering Structure System
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Traditional building structures dissipate seismic energy through the plastic deformation of members in the earthquake, which may lead to a large residual deformation after the earthquake. Those structures are very difficult to repair. Traditional building structure can become a new structure with self-centering ability by using a special energy dissipation component, adding prestressed tendons or supplementing dampers. Compared to the traditional building structure, this new self-centering structure can more effectively reduce the residual deformation caused by the earthquake, and it has a desirable capability to dissipate seismic energy so as to enable itself to be of more security. In this study, the domestic and foreign self-centering structures are classified and summarized. This study deals with research progress of self-centering structures including self-centering braced steel frame structure, self-centering steel plate shear wall structure and self-centering offshore platform structure. Besides, this study introduces the related research progress of other research fellows.

articleTitle: Analysis of Tidal Currents Using Hydrodynamic Model in the Lingding Bay of Pearl River Delta
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: To investigate tidal dynamics in the Lingding Bay (LDB), a three-dimensional (3D) hydrodynamic model for this area was established, and the verification indicates that there is a good agreement between model results and observations for tide levels, tidal current velocities and directions. Modelling results are characterized significantly with tidal current circulation, which reflects the dynamic characteristics at the time of the maximum velocities of flood and ebb tides. This study improves our understanding of estuary dynamics and provides technical supports for the construction of ports, waterways as well as marine development plans in the LDB area.

articleTitle: Research on Limit Equilibrium Analysis Method of Loess Slope Considering Cross-anisotropy
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: By analyzing the relationship between the sliding surface and the principal stress angle in different stress spatial domains, it is assumed that the friction angles on the sliding surface changes in cosine under axisymmetric compression. Put forward A limit equilibrium analysis idea of loess slope considering cross-anisotropic. The equations for determining the safety factor of the Swedish strip method, simplified Bishop method and Spencer method considering the cross-anisotropic are derived. It is verified by an example that this method not only improves the accuracy of slope safety factor calculation, but also conforms to the actual engineering of the loess high slope. Considering the soil anisotropy guidance project for the stability of the actual loess high slopes, it has important theoretical and practical significance.

articleTitle: Intelligent integrated modeling of the hydropower house and its fully coupled transient simulation analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: This paper studies the Computer Aided Design/Computer Aided Engineering (CAD/CAE) based intelligent integrated modeling technology of the hydropower house and the solution method of the fully coupled transient dynamics. Focusing on the modeling difficulty due to the complex multi-curved surface structure of the Francis turbine and double field coupling between fluid and solid, the technologies of fine modeling, integrated assembly and fully coupled simulation of hydraulics-mechanics-structure of the hydropower house are studied. The three-dimensional fluid-hydraulic machinery-concrete structure coupled simulation model is established, including the channel water, mechanical structure of hydro generator unit and concrete structure. The two-way iterative fluid-structure coupling method is adopted for coupling calculation.
