publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Analysis of the temporal distribution characteristics of waves can evaluate the temporal distribution status of regional wave energy resources. In this paper, wave dataset from an offshore wave buoy was used, annual and seasonal variation characteristics of significant wave height and zero-crossing wave period were analyzed. Joint frequency distribution between wave height and wave period was established by using Copula function to analyze their correlations.

articleTitle: Runoff Evolution and Attribution Analysis of Yichang Station under the Impact of Joint Operation of Reservoirs
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The runoff regime had been impacted greatly in the down-stream of Yangtze River because of the joint operation of reservoirs, and the Three Gorges project is the most critical project. Aim to the unreasonable and inconsistent alteration analysis results in the existing runoff regime research with single alteration analysis method, the hydrological alteration diagnosis system was used to the alteration analysis and alteration period identification of measured runoff series at Yichang Hydrological Station, to conclude the evolution characteristics of the runoff regime. And the attribution analysis method with rainfall runoff curves was used to study the main influencing factors within climate change and human activities. The analysis results show that, the alteration existed in 9 series with different alteration degrees at Yichang station, the flood season series showed a downward trend, while the low flow season series showed an upward trend. Attribution analysis shows that, human activities are the main causes of hydrological alteration of runoff series at Yichang Hydrological Station except July.

articleTitle: Experimental study on physical properties of glazed hollow bead ultra high performance concrete
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: An experimental study was carried out on the performance of ultra-high performance concrete (UHPC) containing glaze hollow beads(GHB), and the effects of different amounts of GHB on the fluidity, apparent density, compressive strength, flexural strength and splitting tensile strength of UHPC were analyzed. The results show that when the content of GHB increases in the range of $0\sim2$%, the apparent density of UHPC tends to decrease, the apparent density decreases to 2264kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and the fluidity and strength (compression, bending and splitting tensile) decrease to a certain extent, but the strength loss rate remains in the range of 12% $\sim$ 27%, which basically meets the mechanical index requirements of UHPC. The research conclusions can provide a support for the engineering application of lightweight ultra-high performance concrete.

articleTitle: Study on fuzzy control of magnetorheological dampers in a hydropower house
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a strategy for the vibration control of the hydropower house. The strategy is based on a combination of the fuzzy logic control (FLC) algorithm, magnetorheological (MR) dampers, and the finite element method (FEM). A 3D mechanics-concrete structure coupled simulation model of the Xiangjiaba hydropower house was established in ADINA software. The structural vibration responses of the hydropower house are acquired based on fluid induced vibration method. Bouc-Wen model is established in Simulink to calculate the MR damping force based on FLC algorithm. Real-time update on the damping force assigned to ADINA is realized by MATLAB interface. The study indicates that the proposed method provides more reduction of vibration responses as that obtained by the bang-bang control with less control force and much less command current. The research outcome can provide a scientific reference for structural vibration control of the hydropower house.

articleTitle: CFD Numerical Statistics on Regular Wave Fields
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: This paper describes the finite element algorithm which is devoted to the hydro-dynamic simulation on 2-D regular wave fields. The method hinges on the interpolative function establishment and the statistical computation on the hydro-dynamic characteristics of the shear deformation field. The results show that the turbulent distribution of the velocities causes the certain generation of the suction area where the submarine vessels will confront the disadvantageous hydro-dynamic pressure.

articleTitle: Non-uniform Corrosion Expansion and Bond Analysis of RC Members
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Non-uniform corrosion of steel bars causes concrete cracking in chloride-contaminated reinforced concrete (RC) structures. The degree of surface cracking of the concrete reflects the corrosion intensity of the internal reinforcement. Thus, it is essential to investigate the corrosion and bond performance of RC after cracking. The electrochemical corrosion method was used to assess the influence of steel bar corrosion on the RC specimens. Non-uniform radial displacement of the steel bars was considered, and a non-uniform theoretical model was used to evaluate the cracking behavior of the concrete cover. The corrosion rate of the reinforcement after cracking was quantitatively analyzed. A pull-out test was performed on the RC specimens after expansion cracking, and the relationship between the bond performance and the crack width was analyzed. A method for determining the influence of the crack width on the bond performance was proposed.

articleTitle: Research on the relationship between concrete base temperature difference and length of pouring block in strongly constrained zone
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Reducing the length of concrete pouring blocks is one of the most important measures for temperature control and crack prevention of mass concrete, but there is little exploration of the specific relationship between the temperature drop and the length of concrete pouring blocks. In this paper, the finite element model of different length is established for the concrete block in the strong restraint area of the concrete dam. The maximum concrete base temperature difference that can be withstood by the pouring blocks of strong restraint zone with different lengths is obtained, which can provide a reference for the temperature control index during the concrete pouring process.

articleTitle: Experimental study of slurry reinforcement of saturated soft loess
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The tunnel envelope of saturated soft loess stratum has the characteristics of low strength, poor bearing capacity and weak resistance to deformation. Concealed tunnels through saturated soft loess strata are prone to surface subsidence, ground building tilt damage, bridge deformation and other construction disasters. Therefore, it is important to carry out research on grouting reinforcement of in situ saturated soft loess. In this paper, based on the project of the interval between Guandong Zhengjie and Xingqing Park of Xi’an Metro Line 6, physical property tests, loess splitting and grouting tests and physical and mechanical properties tests of the surrounding rocks of the grouted reinforced test section were conducted on the saturated soft loess. It is concluded that grouting mainly reduces the permeability of the in-situ soil and improves the cohesion of the soil, with small changes to the density and internal friction angle of the soil, and improves the overall shear strength of the soil. Full-section grouting is effective in improving the strength of the surrounding rock and palm face excavation soil.

articleTitle: CFD Numerical Simulation on Regular Wave Fields with 2-D Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The study focused on the numerical development and cyber simulation on the hydro-dynamics of regular wave fields. The applicable mathematical model and algorithm were given and the hydro-dynamical characteristics were computed. The key hydro-dynamical rules on regular wave fields were reported based on the boundary excitation.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Flood Routing for Yihe River with Hydrologic and Hydraulic Model
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The law of flood movement in Yihe river basin is very complex. The flood forecast of Yihe river is studied by using hydrological model in past. The MIKE11 software was used to calculate the flood evolution of Yihe river channel by NAM hydrological model and 1-D hydrodynamic model (HD) in this paper. The calculated results of hydrological model were used as the lateral inflow conditions of HD model. The model parameters were calibrated based on the observed data. The model was verified by field data. The calculated water level and discharged process of Linyi and Gegou hydrology station are basically consistent with the observed data. The efficiency coefficient (NSE) of the model is greater than 0.87.

articleTitle: Construction information management system for rock-filled concrete dam (CIM4R)
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Rock-Filled Concrete (RFC) dam is a new type of concrete dam based on the technology of self-compacting concrete (SCC). To improve the quality control of construction in RFC dam site, a construction information management system for RFC dams (CIM4R) was developed. The software system has two user interfaces. The first is WEB based user interface for PCs, which takes control of the basic project information, the user authorization and data statistical analysis. The second is WeChat based user interface for mobile phones, which is assigned to users for the work stage control, information collection, message notification, and on-site record. Several modules are increasingly developed in the management system, such as inventory and inspection of raw materials, production control in the mixing plant, testing concrete specimens, quality inspection of unit engineering, and so on. AliCloud platform provides the platform for the storage of engineering data.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Water Level Changes in Flood Season at Representative Stations in Taihu Lake Basin in the Process of Urbanization
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Urbanization, as one of the most violent processes for human beings to change the regional underlying surface conditions, has greatly changed the regional water cycle process, especially the impact on flood disasters. Taking the Taihu Lake basin as the research area, using the hydrological variation diagnosis method with multiple variation points identification, the characteristics of the highest and average water level changes during the flood season of Taihu Lake and 8 plain river network representative stations were detected. Overall, except that the maximum water level of CX and HCQ stations has a downward trend, the maximum water level and average water level of Taihu Lake and other representative stations in flood season show an upward trend, and the upward trend of some stations is significant. There are double variation points in representative stations of Lake area and plain river network, and the first variation point is distributed in the 1980s, and the second variation point is concentrated in 2000 $\sim$ 2010.

articleTitle: In-situ Shear Test of RCC Technology for Dahuaqiao Hydropower Station Dam Project
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The selection of interlayer shear strength parameters of RCC is very important for the stability and safety of dam. Because of the characteristic of layered roller compaction, the joint of each layer will become the weak layer in the concrete, which plays a key role in the calculation of anti-slip stability of RCC gravity dam. In this paper, in-situ shear tests of 180d RCC with different interlayer treatment methods were carried out, and the shear strength parameters of different interlayer treatment methods were obtained. The results show that all the interlayer treatment measures and interlayer bonding quality of the RCC test meet the engineering requirements.

articleTitle: Reinforcement effect and mechanism of geogrids in embankment expansion
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The interaction mechanism between geosynthetics and surrounding soil has not been completely illustrated yet. There is still a lack of analysis on the reinforcement effect and mechanism of the geogrids on embankment expansion. Based on a highway embankment expansion project, various geogrid arrangements are simulated through the finite element method and the geogrid reinforcement mechanism is analyzed based on the analysis results. The results show that only increasing the number of geogrid layers has a small effect on the embankment deformation. The geogrids laid at the bottom of the embankment provides a better limit on the soil deformation inside the new embankment. The deformation of geogrids near the embankment surface is more obvious. The geogrids can not only limit soil deformation in horizontal direction through the friction, but also limit soil deformation in vertical direction through the great tensile properties.

articleTitle: Research and application of key technology in construction of steel structure of super-high and large-span heavy duty globular corridor
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: As the appearance design of high-rise curved buildings becomes more and more complicated, the traditional component fabrication and installation technology and the in-situ assembly technology in high altitude are gradually unable to meet the engineering requirements. Based on the project of Intercontinental Hotel in Wuhan International Expo Center, this paper puts forward the steel structure construction technology of super-high and large-span heavy-duty spherical corridor. The key technology mainly consists of four parts: (1) the technology deepens the design of corridor and combines the application of a variety of software to solve the problems of many kinds of components, large quantity and difficult positioning. Through structural design and deepening design of temporary measures, the bearing capacity of temporary measures can be guaranteed to meet the construction requirements and accuracy; (2) special-shaped component fabrication technology. Numerical control machining and computer simulation assisted pre-assembly, which are very intuitive to check the production quality of special-shaped components, are applied to improve accuracy and reduce costs; (3) low level assembly technology. Unsupported assembly method is adopted to solve the problem of insufficient bearing capacity of the site. The reticulated shell components are divided into units first and then into blocks for assembly, which is timesaving, efficient and highly accurate. (4) the overall lifting technology, which counterweights the rear anchor points and ties the front anchor points to the cable and then uses the triangle truss as the lifting frame body, can effectively solve the problems of fewer lifting points and large lifting force of a single point. This technology has important reference significance to the construction of heavy - duty connecting corridor.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Vibration Characteristics of Ship Lift under Xiangjiaba Flood Discharge
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Xiangjiaba ship lift is adjacent to the powerhouse behind the dam on the left bank. During daily operation, it is affected by the operation of the left bank unit and the dam flood discharge during flood discharge, resulting in obvious vibration response in the ship lift area. Xiangjiaba hydropower plant arranges vibration monitoring points at typical parts of ship lift area to study the vibration influence of ship lift area. In this paper, the vibration response data obtained from monitoring are used for analysis and research. It is found that the excellent frequency band of pressure pulsation excitation generated by flood discharge to Xiangjiaba in flood season is 0.3 ~ 11 Hz, which presents the characteristics of narrow-band random vibration. The analysis shows that the flood discharge excitation to Xiangjiaba in flood season does not affect the safety of ship lift tower column structure; through modal analysis, the first and second natural frequencies of the tower structure are 0.94 Hz and 1.04 Hz, and the vibration mode is mainly reflected in horizontal shaking in the cross river direction; the third and fourth order natural frequencies are 2.52 Hz and 2.87 Hz, which are mainly reflected in the horizontal shaking of the tower structure along the river. The main frequency of flood discharge pressure pulsation excitation energy is mainly distributed in the low-frequency band, which can stimulate the first few low-frequency vibrations of Xiangjiaba tower column structure. Therefore, the tower column structure will produce obvious horizontal vibration response during flood discharge.

articleTitle: Analysis on Natural Runoff Effect of NDVI Change in the Yongding River Mountain Area From 1982 to 2015
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Based on the analysis of the temporal and spatial variation of NDVI in Yongding River mountain area, the influence of NDVI variation characters and its effect on the attenuation of natural runoff in Yongding River mountain area is analyzed by using the monitoring data such as NDVI and natural runoff. The results show that NDVI in Yongding River mountain area increased significantly from 1982 to 2015, and it presented a certain spatial heterogeneity. The natural runoff of the hydrological stations in YRMA also has a significant attenuation trend. Through Budyko hypothesis analysis, it is found that the variation of natural runoff is highly sensitive to NDVI change. As NDVI change being the prominent feature in the role of natural runoff attenuation, great attention should be paid to the impact of vegetation protection and soil and water conservation on the natural runoff attenuation in Yongding River mountain area.

articleTitle: Application of Smart Site Construction Technology in Civil Airport Airfield Area
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The civil airport airfield area project has the characteristics of large construction scale, long construction period, involving many professionals, and high construction quality requirements. The traditional airport airfield area construction management method is difficult to effectively manage the quality, safety, equipment, information, and environment during the construction process, and there are problems such as low management efficiency, poor informationization, and difficulty in adapting to environmental protection requirements. With the rapid development of IoT technology, big data technology, BIM technology and cloud computing technology, smart construction sites have emerged. This article introduces the smart site construction technology in civil airport airfield area from the aspect of key technologies and airport airfield area smart construction site management platform. The intelligent construction site management platform of the civil airport airfield area is the core of the intelligent construction site. The intelligent construction site platform system of the airport airfield area realizes the scientific and precise management of engineering projects through the use of information technology. It has the functions of quality management, safety management, equipment management, information management, environmental management and video monitoring during the construction process. The use of the smart construction site platform can guarantee the construction quality of the airport airfield area, improve the efficiency of construction management, and bring great social and economic benefits.

articleTitle: Research on New Type of Cement-soil Piles to Reinforce Soft Soil Foundation
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The new type of cement-soil pile (NCSP) is an environmentally friendly pile, which compulsorily mixes the soil and curing agent outside the in-situ foundation. During the mixing process, a certain amount of construction waste can be used to form a homogeneous plastic pile while forming a hole. Based on the standard penetration test (SPT) and the unconfined compressive strength test, the variation law of the standard penetration test and the unconfined compressive strength(q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf>) along the depth of the pile is discussed, established the correlation between the number of standard penetration test and the unconfined compressive strength. The difference between the theoretical value and the measured value of the composite foundation bearing capacity is clarified. The results show that the standard penetration stroke and the unconfined compressive strength are uniformly distributed along the depth, and the two have a good linear relationship. The unconfined compressive strength increases with the increase of the cement content. The pile type can meet the requirements of the engineering. It has good engineering characteristics for construction needs.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on the Effect of Ultrasonic Plug Removal Technology of Dike Relief Wells
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Relief wells are important seepage control measures to prevent seepage failures of levees. However, the efficiency of relief wells decreases with time due to blockage of well filter and screens. It is essential to take remedial measures to improve relief well performance for disaster prevention and mitigation function. This paper develops an ultrasonic plugging removal system which is suitable for dike relief well. The process of backward silting of the relief well is simulated in a large laboratory permeameter, and the self-developed ultrasonic equipment is used to remove the plug. The performance of the proposed ultrasonic technology is studied through the constant water head permeation test. The experimental results show that the proposed ultrasonic removal technology can significantly improve the drainage capacities of clogged relief wells in the sand confined aquifer foundation. The plugging degree of relief wells and performance of ultrasonic plugging increase with the decrease of confined aquifer sand density. The density of confined aquifer sand sample has a significant effect on the ultrasonic treatment time. The ultrasonic treatment time should be controlled within 60 min and 90 min for the confined aquifer sand density ρ = 1.45 g/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and ρ = 1.50 g/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis of Bearing Capacity and Buckling Stability of Large-scale Corrugated Steel Webs
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: With the development of PC composite box girder Bridges with corrugated steel webs, it is urgent to study the mechanical properties of large corrugated steel webs with larger span. In this paper, the bearing capacity and buckling stability of 2000 and 2400 corrugated steel webs are studied by means of finite element simulation. Through the finite element simulation analysis under three loading modes, it is concluded that the buckling load of 2000 and 2400 corrugated steel webs is greater than the ultimate load, and the shear capacity and buckling stability of 2000 and 2400 corrugated steel webs are better than that of 1600. Geometric parameters are important factors affecting the bearing capacity and buckling stability of corrugated steel webs.

articleTitle: Research on Integration of Solar Heating Technology for Rural Self-Sufficiency House in Cold Areas Take Beijing and surrounding areas as an example
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Under the guidance of the national clean heating policy, the winter heating methods in cold rural areas need to be updated urgently. Taking rural solar heating technology as target, this paper puts forward the concept of heating technology integration. After analyzing the current status and problems of solar heating technology applied to rural houses, this paper also discusses the key points of design and integration between self-sufficiency houses and solar heating technology from active and passive solar heating technology. Finally, there are reasonable suggestions for the selection of heating technology for the self-sufficiency houses.

articleTitle: Study on External Pressure Buckling of Penstock in Hydropower Station Based on Eigenvalue Stability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to study the external pressure buckling feature of penstock in hydropower station, a penstock was taken as the research object and the eigenvalue stability analysis method was used. The influence of different working conditions on the change of stress and displacement were studied, and the critical value of local buckling of penstock to withstand uniformly distributed radial pressure was given. The results show that the maximum circumferential stress and Mises stress on the pipe wall appear at the junction of the steel pipe and the stiffening ring, respectively; the cross section of the deformed steel pipe is oval, and the maximum displacement occurs at the pipe waist or pipe top. The critical value of local buckling of penstock is 0.173 MPa. The research results are helpful for the design of penstock.

articleTitle: Study on impact resistance of fiber-reinforced recycled concrete slab based on ABAQUS
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In this paper, ABAQUS numerical simulation is used to study the impact resistance of waste fiber recycled concrete slab with 50% replacement rate of recycled aggregates and 0.08% and 0.12% volume addition of waste fibers. The impact times at the initial crack of RC50, RC50-0.08, and RC50-0.12 are 10, 17, and 21 times respectively. With the increase of the volume of waste fibers, the impact resistance of recycled concrete slabs is enhanced. The addition of waste fibers inhibits the development of cracks under impact force, to improve the impact resistance.

articleTitle: Research on the key technology of repairing the defect of highway pier
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Taking the practical project as an example, this paper puts forward the corresponding repair scheme for the shortcoming of the concrete strength of highway bridge pier body. Designed the treatment process and structure of the pier column chiseling and replacement scheme, and analyzes the bearing capacity of the pier, the reliability of the steel pipe support and the stress safety of the whole bridge structure after the treatment by the finite element calculation. The research shows that the scheme has no influence on the whole and local force safety of the whole bridge, and has strong reliability. With a view to provide reference for similar projects.

articleTitle: Permeability characteristic and microstructure analysis of bentonite cement composite sand
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Seepage, a common problem in underground projects, seriously affects the safety and durability of underground structures. Grouting is a common means to achieve seepage prevention and plugging in underground spaces, and bentonite cement-based grout is a kind of grouting material with good performance. In this paper, with variable head permeability tests, the permeability characteristic of bentonite cement composite sand is analyzed, which shows that the bentonite cement-based grout can reduce the permeability coefficient of sand to a large extent and the plugging effect of micro fine cement is better than that of ordinary cement under the same conditions. The microstructure is analyzed by scanning electron microscope tests. The test results show that the CSH gel produced by cement hydration can link with bentonite to form a dense microstructure, which is attached to the surface of sand grains and fills the pores between sand grains, thus reducing the permeability of the sand and achieving seepage prevention and plugging.

articleTitle: 3D numerical manifold method with partially overlapping covers based on hexahedron covers
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Numerical Manifold Method (NMM) with partially overlapping covers is a new method based on independent covers analysis, which is limited to two-dimension problems currently. Analysis of high - low mixed order 3D NMM with partially overlapping covers is carried out via construction of partially overlapping system based on hexahedron mesh and by using freedom constraint between nodes, so the corresponding element matrix formula is given and numerical examples shows the validity of the method. The results show that computation degree of freedom is greatly reduced when the accuracy requirement is satisfied. In some concerned independent cover areas such as dam heel, the improvement of calculation accuracy caused by the upgrading of independent cover function or encrypted cover is obvious, and has little impact on the calculation results in the surrounding cover.

articleTitle: Rheologic and microscopic characteristics of nano layered silicate grout for underground water leakage control
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Nanomaterial provides a new method for underground water leakage control whereby nanoparticle suspensions are slowly injected and transported through the groundwater flow into the target position. This is a new method different from traditional cement grouting. The material properties of the nanomaterial grout strongly influence the effectiveness of grouting process by the nanoparticles. This paper conducted viscosity tests and Cryo-scanning electron microscope (Cryo-SEM) to investigate the viscosity growth rule and microstructure of nanomaterial grout for soil treatment. Laponite was selected as the representative nano layered silicate. Possible solution concentrations and gel time are analysed precisely. The moderate concentrations (2.5-3.5%) with gel time (5-7 days) are more appropriate for laponite grout. In addition, the direct micrograph of laponite grout with different concentrations was also achieved. The results can establish viscosity and microscopic structure characterization description of laponite grout, and will benefit the practical implementation of this method of water leakage control.

articleTitle: Design and construction control of single tower cable-stayed bridge without backstays
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Cable-stayed bridge without backstays has great architectural aesthetic feeling in bridge design, and embodies the perfect combination of force and beauty in bridge type. It has been built in landscape bridges all over the world. The shape of cable-stayed bridge without backstays determines that its stress characteristics are different from those of conventional cable-stayed bridges, and the key points of bridge design and construction control are also different. Taking a (30+120+40)m three-span cable-stayed bridge without backstays as an example, this paper introduces the design originality, structural layout and design features of the bridge, and analyzes the control points that should be paid attention to in bridge construction, which provides guidance for bridge construction.

articleTitle: Variation Characteristics of Extreme Precipitation in the Shiwulihe River Basin in Hefei
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Due to the influence of climate warming and human activities, extreme precipitation events occur frequently in various parts of the country. In order to reduce their negative impacts, the present study envisaged a systematic and comprehensive analysis of the variation characteristics in extreme precipitation of the Shiwulihe River Basin. Based on the daily precipitation data of the Shiwulihe River Basin in Hefei from 1960 to 2019, six extreme precipitation indexes such as RX1day, RX5day, R20 mm, R95P, SDII and CWD were selected. The variation characteristics in the extreme precipitation were analyzed using linear trend analysis, M-K non-parametric test, sliding T test, Morlet continuous complex wavelet analysis, and Pearson correlation analysis. The results reveal the time-varying characteristics of extreme precipitation in Shiwulihe River Basin.

articleTitle: Experimental analysis on construction mechanical properties of parallel rectangular pipe jacking based on similar model test
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: According to a parallel rectangular pipe jacking project, a model test research was carried out based on the similarity theory. And the vertical deformation of the surface, earth pressure and pipe strain are discussed in the process of parallel rectangular pipe jacking construction, to analyze the interaction of parallel rectangular pipe jacking construction and the soil layer disturbance effect. The research shows that: 1) the surface settlement value increases gradually when the first pipe is jacked, and the settlement value tends to be stable, but the final settlement value of the first pipe decreases slightly when the second pipe is jacked, and the center of the surface settlement trough shifts from the first pipe to the second pipe. The settlement value at the second pipe is slightly less than that of the first pipe, so the jacking sequence of the parallel pipe should be reasonably selected during construction. 2) With the jacking of pipe, the earth pressure value above the pipe jacking increases first and then decreases. The pipe jacking can reduce the vertical soil pressure under the pipe jacking to a certain extent. In the process of pipe jacking, the excavation amount of soil in the pipe should be set reasonably to control the earth pressure on pipe jacking. 3) In the process of pipe jacking construction, the maximum strain of pipe appears at different positions, which indicates that uneven jacking force will lead to local stress concentration of pipe. Effective measures should be taken to control the jacking attitude of pipe and real-time monitoring should be strengthened. Relevant research results can provide a reference for rectangular pipe jacking design and construction.

articleTitle: Modeling and analyzing of waterlogging in typical urban area
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: With the acceleration of urbanization, urban waterlogging has become a difficult problem, which restricts the sustainable development and urbanization in China. This paper evaluates, analyzes and summarizes the current waterlogging research in China from three aspects: waterlogging control standards, waterlogging control models and methods, and current research difficulties. We take the Jiangbei District, Fuzhou City as an example. A waterlogging model was established to obtain the stage hydrographs and design flood flow, comprehensively evaluating the waterlogging situation and the comprehensive waterlogging prevention capacity. The results show that, accurate waterlogging simulation plays an important role in the construction of urban waterlogging prevention. While addressing the existing controllable difficulties, the research on urban waterlogging in China should actively work on coping strategies for uncontrollable difficulties, and enhance the ability of the regional waterlogging management system to deal with various extreme weather conditions and human activities.

articleTitle: Magnetism-mechanics Performance of Magnetically Controlled Shape Memory Alloy and Application For Active Control System
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: To control the dynamic stability of light steel structure, magnetism-mechanics performance of magnetically controlled shape memory alloy (MSMA) was studied, the MSMA actuator and MSMA active control system was developed. The material properties of MSMA related to magnetism and mechanics was studied, at the same time, the influence of the Ni-Mn-Ga contained in MSMA on the magnetism-mechanics properties was analysed, Ni<inf>53</inf>Mn<inf>25</inf>Ga<inf>22</inf> was selected to build the design theoretical basis of MSMA actuator. Taking three MSMA rods with a size of 4x8x45mm as the core element, a new type of actuator was developed, and the corresponding magnetism-mechanics performance test was carried out. The key factors such as magnetic field, de-formation rate, preloading, active control force, etc. were determined, as well as the mathematical models with the changes of parameters were established. The controlled object (steel truss model structure), MSMA actuator, control algorithm, data acquisition system, etc. constitute the MSMA active control system. Two MSMA actuators are installed on the steel truss model structure, under the excitation of sine wave, the dynamic response of the steel truss model structure with the MSMA active control system was tested, and the results was compared with uncontrolled; The results show that the acceleration response of the steel truss model structure equipped with the MSMA active control system decreased by about 25%, and the displacement response decreased by about 20%. The active control system with MSMA actuator as the core component can better realize the dynamic stability control of steel structure.

articleTitle: Machine learning-based algorithm for predicting the groundwater level in Minqin Oasis region of China
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been widely used in the prediction of groundwater level, but most of these models are incapable of screening and analyzing the types of input variables, and fail to further explore the nonlinear interactions between these input variables and the degree of their influence on groundwater level. To solve the above-mentioned problems, a GRA-FA-SVM hybrid model, which combines the support vector machine (SVM) with the grey relational analysis (GRA) and the factor analysis (FA), was established to predict the groundwater level. The relevant field observation data at two observation wells in Minqin County of northwestern China was used for validating the proposed hybrid model. The investigated results verify the effectiveness of the hybrid model and show that the GRA-FA-SVM model gives the highest accuracy.

articleTitle: Whole Chain based Adaptive Risk Management: A system approach to improve Urban Water Resilience
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: With the development of urbanization in China, the problem of urban waterlogging has become increasingly prominent. The lack of systematic management system design is an important factor to this water problem. From the point of view of system analysis, a whole chain based adaptive risk management framework is systematically presented to improve urban water resilience. It includes three interactive chains, including actively reduce risk beforehand, i.e., risk aversion, risk warning and risk diversification (chain 1), dynamically assess risk in the process, i.e., risk tracking and risk management (chain 2), as well as flexibly respond to risk after the event, i.e., emergency response and maintenance & feedback (chain 3). These three chains are interacted with each other, and the chain 3 feeds back to the chain 1 to promote the overall improvement of the system. With application to case study city, this system approach is proved to be effective and helpful.

articleTitle: Future drought projection of Southwestern China based on CMIP5 model and MCI index
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In the past 50 years, Southwestern China has suffered from frequent, intense droughts. MCI (meteorological drought composite index) was calculated, and ArcGIS Spatial Analyst was run in the present study. The simulation performance was compared between different CMIP5 models. Then we projected the temporal and spatial distributions of drought in the intermediate path (RCP4.5 scenario) in the two time periods (2018-2058 and 2059-2099) between 2018 and 2099. The results showed that (1) the number of days with moderate drought and above increased in Southwestern China in both two time periods. The high-value regions were mainly found at the borders between Sichuan and Yunnan Province from 2018 to 2099. The annual number of drought days was generally above 150d. The low-value regions were mainly found in some parts of southeastern Sichuan, Chongqing, and the large parts of Guizhou. The annual average number of drought days was generally below 100d; (2) At phase P1 (from 2018 to 2058), the projected spatial distribution of drought severity was generally consistent with that of the annual average number of days with moderate drought and above. At phase P2 (from 2059 to 2099), the high-value regions of drought severity were still primarily found at the borders between Sichuan and Yunnan Province. The low-value regions were mainly found in the large parts of Chongqing and Guizhou. As time progressed, the high-value regions of drought severity expanded, and the drought was aggravated; (3) At phase P1, the high-value regions of drought frequency were mainly found at the borders between Sichuan and Yunnan. In these regions, the drought frequency was above 80%. The low-value regions of drought frequency were mainly found in parts of western Guizhou and central and eastern Sichuan. In these regions, the drought frequency was below 20%. At phase P2, the high-value regions of drought frequency were generally found in Yunnan Province and southwestern Sichuan. In these regions, the drought frequency was above 60%. The low-value regions of drought frequency were mainly found in Chongqing and northern Guizhou. In these regions, the drought frequency was below 20%. From phase P1 to P2, the high-value regions of drought frequency expanded, and the drought frequency increased. The low-value regions of drought frequency shrank in size. The drought frequency also decreased. Taken together, the drought in Southwestern China was aggravated and occurred more frequently according to the projections from 2018 to 2099. Our research findings offered important guidance for drought early warning and prevention in Southwestern China.

articleTitle: Influence of unsupported length on underground cavity stability in sandstone stratum with weak interlayer
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The unsupported length has great influence on the stability of an underground cavity when constructing it in sandstone stratum with weak interlayer. To provide guidance for safe construction, the physical and mechanical parameters of sandstone are tested first, and then a numerical model considering the weak interlayer is established by using 3DEC to analyze the influence of unsupported length. It is found that the strength of slightly weathered sandstone with medium coarse grain is in the range of 59.5-116MPa, and the saturated compressive strength will reduce greatly. When there is little difference in the internal mineral composition, the strength reduction of rock sample shows a positive correlation with water absorption, while the elastic modulus and the Poisson’s ratio are less affected by it. Meanwhile, the tensile strength is about 1.25% of its compressive strength. The unsupported length has an impact on the disturbed zone of surrounding rock mass. The shorter unsupported length can reduce the deformation of surrounding rock mass, and the reasonable excavation footage should not be greater than 6m. The stress of bolt below the rock anchoring beam is great although the unsupported length has little impact on the stress change of bolt at this position. One thing should be point out is that the bolt stress at the weak interlayer is obviously greater than that in the vault, and the strength of support here should be strengthened.

articleTitle: The Chaos of the Prediction for Tailings Pond Dam Break Disasters
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Tailings pond is a special geotechnical structure. It is of great significance to carry out the analysis and study of the monitoring data on tailings ponds to improve the prediction and early warning of tailings dam breaks and prevent tailings dam accidents. Based on the analysis of the basic structure of the monitoring system, the data on the displacement of the tailings dam is deeply studied using chaos theory from the perspective of non-linear dynamical systems. By compiling the software under the MATLAB environment, we obtain the Lyapunov exponent as well as the calculation method for the correlation dimension D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> of the dynamical characteristics of the tailings pond system. The monitoring data obtained from the actual measurement is used for studying the prediction of tailings dam breaks. The prediction results show that there are non-integral dimensions and positive maximum Lyapunov exponents in the displacement evolution of the tailings dam, and that the minimum factor needed for describing the displacement evolution is greater than 3, which indicates that tailings dam is a very complex non-linear dynamical system. The maximum Lyapunov exponent can be used as an index for evaluating the displacement changes.

articleTitle: Emergy-based environmental accounting and analysis of the floodplain of the Lower Yellow River
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The floodplain ecosystem has attracted much attention because of its great benefits in river water and sediment transportion, water environment and ecology protection, regional economic development. Different from the existing research, an emergy-based environmental accounting and analysis for the floodplain of the Lower Yellow River has been presented in this paper. The types and characteristics of the floodplain ecosystem services have been clarified. The process of emergy input-output in the floodplain of the Lower Yellow River has been analyzed. According to them, the value of ecosystem services in the floodplain of the Lower Yellow River in 2015 has been accounted. Then, based on Emergy evaluation indices, the potential sustainability has been valued. Analytical results show that, the total emergy inflow for the floodplain ecosystem of the Lower Yellow River in 2015 is 1.15E+22sej, and the total emergy outflow is 6.32E+21sej. In emergy inflow, the feedback emergy ratio is 48.77%, and the renewable emergy ratio is 25.14%. The emergy density of the ecosystem is 4.16E+12sej/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, yet emergy per capital is 7.95E+15sej/capita, which are very low compared to the whole Yellow River Basin. The emergy yield ratio is 1.12, the emergy investment ratio is 0.92, which are also less than that of the Yellow River Basin. It implies that the development level of the Floodplain of the Lower Yellow River is very low and mainly depends on natural resources. The emergy self-support ratio of the ecosystem is 0.51, the environment load ratio is 2.98 and the emergy sustainable indice is 0.38. It indicates that the development potential is very large.

articleTitle: Research on Assessment of Earthquake Liquefaction in Offshore Wind Turbine Based on Dynamic Triaxial Test
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Considering the obviously distinctive methods for liquefaction assessment of cohesiveless soils both at home and abroad, this paper compares and summarizes the available methods for assessing the earthquake liquefaction in offshore wind power applications in current stage. Taking an offshore wind power farm project in eastern Guangdong as an example, the simplified SEED method is adopted to assess the liquefaction of soil masses with the laboratory triaxial test based on the survey and drilling data at typical wind turbine positions on the site. Different soil layers, buried depths, relative densities, and confining pressures are considered in the test. This paper plots the relation curve between the dynamic shear stress ratio and the failure vibration frequency of soil samples under the action of cyclic stresses with a constant amplitude, defines the liquefaction resistance index CRR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf>, and obtains the liquefaction assessment results by comparing the CRR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf> with the calculated CSR according to the seismic design requirements. Besides, the paper also compares the dynamic triaxial test results with the liquefaction assessment results upon the specification approach at the field survey site, showing that both results are substantially identical. These findings may be used for guiding the seismic analysis and foundation structure design on the site of the wind power farm project.

articleTitle: The Assessment of Water Resources Security in Ningxia Based on Ecological Footprint Model
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Regarding the gross water resources security and sustainable development in Ningxia, water resources ecological footprint model (EFw model) is adopted to analyze the temporal and spatial variations of EFw and threshold changing trends of available water resources in Ningxia. The research demonstrate that the period from 2002 to 2019 witnessed a decrease in fluctuation of EFw, a high year-to-year variability of water resources ecological carrying capacity (ECw), and a high supply pressure. On the whole, the water resource utilization efficiency has a remarkble improvement. The water-saving effect of is also conspicuous in agriculture and industry, but urban water consumption is conspicuously increased. In the aspect of space, the water resources ecological footprint in Ningxia is mainly concentrated in Yinchuan and Wuzhong, where water consumption in agriculture is large. In accordance to the macro water resources allocation of the Yellow River, Ningxia’s macro water resources are still in loss, while the ecological losses of macro water resources in Wuzhong and Zhongwei are more serious. Therefore, the improvement of agricultural and industrial water utilization efficiency in accordance to water supply and demand is necessary; besides, the problem of low efficiency of water consumption in tertiary industry and residents also needs to be addressed; lastly, the adjustment of the industrial structure and water resources allocation, and implement practical and effective methods are both essential. Guided by ‘determining city development and industries by water’, the goal of the water resources sustainable development in Ningxia will be realized.

articleTitle: Study on Data Mining and Intelligent Early Warning of Water Dispatch for the South-to-North Water Diversion Middle Route Project
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The South-to-North Water Diversion Middle Route Project is mainly open channel, the line is long, there are many risk sources along the line, and the water dispatch technology is difficult. It is great significant to deeply excavate the dispatch regulations and establish the intelligent early warning models by the modern information processing technology to ensure safe and stable water diversion. Considering the advantages of information diffusion technology in dealing with incomplete sample data, the regression model of radial basis function neural network based on information diffusion is proposed and applied to the analysis and calculation of discharge in water dispatch. Before calculating by neural network, the training sample data are fuzzed by information diffusion to improve the generalization ability of the model. The information diffusion approximate reasoning model is used to clean the real-time data. On the basis of data treatment by information diffusion, the multi-directional intelligent early warning model including water level, flow and opening is established to timely find the abnormalities in the dispatch process and trigger the alarm. The results show that: the regression model suggested based on information diffusion and neural network can smooth the sample data better, and has high fitting accuracy and prediction ability. The intelligent dispatch early warning model can automatically and accurately capture the abnormalities of various early warning factors and give the corresponding alarms to ensure timely response in case of emergencies.

Author Keywords: South-to-North Water Diversion Middle Route Project

articleTitle: Probabilistic method of two-dimensional soil profile based on surface wave exploration
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Two-dimensional soil layers profile inversion is usually based on the in-situ test and borehole information, such as the cone penetration test, standard penetration test, borehole data, which can provide one dimensional data along the depth direction. There are some methods proposed to predict the horizontal soil layers profile, such as Kriging interpolation method, sequential indicator simulation method and Markov chain simulation. However, there may be unknown soil types between adjacent boreholes, so it is impossible to accurately predict two-dimensional soil profile based on interpolation method. This paper proposed a two-dimensional soil layer profile inversion method based on surface wave exploration.

articleTitle: Parameter calibration of VIC model based on intelligent algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The parameters of the hydrological model are important parts of the model, and parameter calibration plays a key role in the output of the model. To analyze the influence of different calibration methods on the simulation results of the VIC hydrological model, the parameter calibration methods are coupled with the VIC model combining the characteristics of the Qinhuai River Basin. Three automatic optimization methods, including the genetic algorithm, simulated annealing algorithm and SCE-UA(shuffle complex evolution algorithm) algorithm, are used to automatically calibrate the 6 parameters of the VIC model. Three evaluation methods of the Nash efficiency coefficient (NSE), mean square error (MSE) and percentage deviation (PBIAS) are used to optimize the parameters. The model’s simulated runoff results are compared and analyzed. The results show that the SCE-UA algorithm with the Nash efficiency coefficient as the objective function can make the VIC model parameter calibration achieve ideal results. Different objective functions have different effects on the peak runoff during the model simulation verification period. By optimizing the parameters with the Nash efficiency coefficient and mean square error as objective functions, the simulated peak runoff is more similar to the measured data. The results can provide a reference for other models parameters automatic calibration, and are of great practical significance for rapid emergency response of hydrological simulation and forecasting.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Operational Tunnel Structure Disease Prediction Based on Graph Attention Network
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: With the rapid development of underground engineering in China, more and more subway tunnels have been built, the operation mileage of subway tunnels has been on the rise, and the corresponding tunnel structure diseases have become increasingly prominent. At present, tunnel structure diseases are mainly treated by manual inspection and identification, and the research on disease prediction is still inadequate. Because of the complexity of factors leading to tunnel structure diseases, it is difficult to analyze the causes and development trends of diseases comprehensively via manual analysis. In addition, over recent years, deep learning has achieved great success in extracting data features (for classification and prediction), and applying deep learning algorithms to graph data is one of the most popular research directions currently. In this paper, graph attention network is introduced into tunnel structure disease prediction for the first time. Based on the characteristics of tunnel structure safety data, a spatio-temporal network is constructed, and the graph attention network is trained to predict the development trend of tunnel structure disease, which provides a new idea for tunnel disease prevention and control. In engineering practice, abundant tunnel structure safety data (68055 ring tunnel segments) were taken as the research object, both the prediction precision and recall rate of the trained model are over 80%, and the prediction results can help with auxiliary decision-making of tunnel maintenance departments and relevant government supervision departments to prevent and control tunnel structure diseases, which focus on tunnel sections where serious diseases may occur, thus further clarifying the development trend of tunnel diseases.

articleTitle: Analysis of Seismic Fragility of Steel-frame structures Built at Different Ages
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In recent decades, the construction industry developed rapidly in China. Due to the large time span of the construction industry development, the design codes that the design and construction of existing buildings relied on are different. However, there are relatively few studies on the seismic capacity of structures designed specifically based on the old version of Chinese code for seismic design of buildings. Once earthquake and other disasters occur, it will be very difficult to assess the damage state of such buildings in time. Based on Chinese Code for Seismic Design of Buildings (GBJ1-89) and Chinese Code for Seismic Design of Buildings (GB50011-2001), this paper designs eight high-rise non-residential steel frames in consideration of different seismic fortification intensities. Based on the IDA analysis method, the seismic vulnerability of eight steel-frame structures is compared in detail. The research results provide a reference for the seismic performance evaluation, earthquake damage state prediction of steel-frame structures design based on different version of seismic design codes, and the revision of seismic design codes.

Author Keywords: comparison of different seismic design code

articleTitle: Erosion Mechanism of Dam Lands and Flow Characteristics of Dam Breaks under Check-Dam-Break Conditions
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The study of water-sediment processes and dam-land-erosion mechanisms under check dam break conditions is of great significance for the construction and later management of check dams. This paper, adopting literature research, field investigation and numerical calculations, identified the main causes of check dam failures, including floods from over-standard precipitation, the lack of backbone engineering within the dam system, the siltation and the like, which lead to insufficient flood detention capacity of the dam, poor construction quality and imperfect operation and management system, etc. It then proposed that the process of dam erosions and gully erosions after check dam failures was as follows: “check dam failure → retrogressive erosion → scouring and undercutting → collapse of gully walls → mixed flow of water and sand”. The water-sand process under the condition of check dam failures was significantly changed by the siltation of the reservoir areas, and the dam lands have the role of shaving peaks and sinking sands.

articleTitle: Research on dam foundation deformation prediction based on VMD optimized temporal convolutional network
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The deformation behavior of the dam foundation directly determines the overall safety of the dam body, especially in the impoundment period and early operation stage of the dam, so it is particularly important to predict and study the displacement of the dam foundation. In order to further improve the accuracy and reliability of dam foundation deformation prediction, VMD (Variational Mode Decomposition) is used to decompose the displacement monitoring time series, and the trend component of displacement and induced component of displacement are obtained. Through the analysis method of time-lag cross-correlation, the dynamic MIC (Maximal information coefficient) between input and output sequences is calculated, the problem of time-lag of displacement monitoring data in the learning and training process is solved, and the length of input time-series variables is determined. Through the iterative learning and training of the trend component and the induced component by TCN (Temporal Convolutional Network), the fitting model functions of the two are obtained respectively, and then the prediction components of the two can be obtained. The classification sum of the two is the final displacement prediction value. The results of case study showed that VMD-TCN prediction model has higher prediction accuracy of dam foundation displacement than ARIMA (Auto Regressive Integrated Moving Average) prediction model, and can better evaluate the future evolution state of dam foundation deformation.

articleTitle: Radiation energy conversion and cooling of concrete box beam based on liquid-gas phase change material
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Concrete is a material with poor thermal conductivity. Under the action of solar radiation, the difference of the concrete box girder in temperatures is too large, resulting in temperature stress, which is likly to cause damage to the structure. Avoiding excessive temperature stress in concrete has always been a problem that people are committed to solving. Based on previous research and the energy storage characteristics of phase change materials, this paper proposes a method of converting solar radiation energy into concrete box girder to cool down, compares and analyzes different types of phase change materials and packaging method. It uses liquid gas phase change material, selects liquid water as the working medium and copper pipe as the packaging material, adds water into the concrete in a large-volume packaging method to adjust the temperature of the concrete box girder, which can reduce the temperature difference between the inside and outside and the harm of temperature stress.

articleTitle: Disaster risk analysis of railway engineering construction in southwest mountainous area based on double-layer network model
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: As the most complex area in topography, geology and geomorphology in the world, the mountainous area in southwest China has been greatly restricted in its traffic development and is the weak place of railway engineering construction in China. In order to promote the economic development of southwest mountainous areas, the traffic construction in this area is imminent. By collecting the data of natural disasters in southwest mountainous areas in the recent 6 years, this paper constructs a double-layer network model with Python. The upper layer is the disaster type and the lower layer is the location along the railway project in southwest mountainous areas. The experimental cases in this paper analyze the disaster types with high frequency and serious impact along the project, the locations seriously affected and the risk chain formed by the disaster, it provides a reference for the safety prevention of railway construction in the future.

articleTitle: Reflection and transmission of waves at a porous-medium/water interface
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Studying the reflection and transmission characteristics of acoustic waves at the porous medium-water interface is of great significance to the inversion of underwater medium parameters and geotechnical engineering detection. The reflection and transmission problems of longitudinal waves incident on the water-porous medium interface from water have been solved. The theoretical research on the incidence of longitudinal waves and shear waves from the porous medium to the porous medium-water interface is still incomplete. Based on the acoustic theory of saturated porous media, the wave potential function and amplitude relationship of each mode are given. Combining the displacement and stress boundary conditions of the fluid and the porous medium, the calculation formulas for the wave reflection and transmission coefficients of each mode are respectively derived when the two waves are incident from the porous medium to the water interface. Taking the sediment porous medium as the research object, the propagation characteristics of longitudinal waves and SV waves from the sediment incident to the water boundary are calculated. The reflection and transmission coefficients changing with incident angle, frequency and porosity are calculated numerically. The calculation results show that the three parameters have different degrees of influence on the reflection and transmission coefficients.

articleTitle: Structural optimization design of mobile flood wall based on improved genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: With the rapid development of human society, urban waterlogging is more and more serious, a flood control facility with convenient transportation and quick installation is urgently needed in the city’s development, which makes the mobile flood wall came into being. The research on mobile flood wall at home and abroad mainly focuses on the analysis of mechanical properties and anti-seepage ability, but in order to improve the utilization rate of material strength and make it more economical, the structure optimization of flood wall is also very important. In this paper, the structural form and the basic parameters of the mobile flood wall are introduced. The finite element model of the mobile flood wall is established and the numerical simulation is carried out on the basis of the constitutive relation. The sample space is obtained by the response value analysis through numerical simulation and the structural parameters are optimized based on the genetic algorithm. In this paper, there are two types of numerical simulation analysis: diagonal bracing and non-diagonal bracing. The simulation analysis shows that the maximum stress of the diagonal bracing is 15. 4MPa, which is less than that of the without diagonal bracing (57. 6MPa), and the maximum displacement of the diagonal bracing is 0.4mm, which is far less than that of the without diagonal bracing (3. 18mm). Both of them meet the safety requirements of the mobile flood wall that the stress δ≤110MPa, the deflection of the main component γ ≤L /250, and the deflection of the baffle γ ≤ L /200.On the basis of numerical simulation, the function constraints of stress, deflection and cost are set by genetic algorithm to optimize the structure. According to the results of numerical analysis, no matter in the column or baffle, the Y-direction displacement value of the form with diagonal bracing is small, and the Y-direction displacement with diagonal bracing baffle is progressive to both sides, which is easier to control in the practical engineering. The analysis shows that the form with the diagonal bracing is far better than that without the diagonal bracing. In the case of the diagonal bracing, the optimization results show that when the height of flood control wall column is 1.0m-1.6m, the span length of baffle is required to be 2.15m-1.91m, which can meet the safety requirements and economic needs, and the optimization scheme is provided for the parameter design and structure design of actual engineering.

articleTitle: Research on Urban Flooding Scenario Simulation of Nantai Island Based on Urban Hydrology and Hydrodynamic Coupling
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Aiming at the frequent occurrence of urban flooding under typhoon and rain on Nantai Island in Fuzhou City, based on the InfoWorks ICM model software, a urban flooding model coupled with urban hydrology, one-dimensional pipe canal hydrodynamics and two-dimensional surface hydrodynamics on Nantai Island was established. After calibrating and verifying the model based on the measured water accumulation under the two typhoon rains of “Sudiruo” and “Catfish”, the load status of the pipe network, the total overflow of inspection wells, and the surface of Nantai Island during the 7 rainstorm return periods Simulation analysis is performed on the range, depth and duration of stagnant water. Under the two typhoon storms, the average error between the simulated and measured water depths was 4.42% and 12.70%, and the simulated water range was consistent with the statistical water depth. Under different rainstorm recurrence periods, the urban flooding simulation results show that the rainstorm recurrence period below 3a and 3a, the area of the whole area is less than 3.62km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the overall drainage capacity of Nantai Island is better; the rainstorm recurrence period of 5a, the whole area The area of stagnant water is 4.95km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the drainage system is close to saturation, and some areas exceed the design standards; the recurrence period of heavy rains in 10a and 10a, the area of stagnant water exceeds 8.82km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the new rainwater no longer enters the drainage system, and all the ground is stored. With the continuous increase of rain intensity, the inspection wells in some areas overflowed seriously. The analysis results can provide theoretical basis and decision support for the prevention and control of urban flooding in Nantai Island.

articleTitle: Analysis of The Spatial and Temporal Distribution Patterns of Rainfall in Shenzhen
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The differences in the spatial and temporal distribution of urban rainfall are related to the deployment of urban flood control and disaster mitigation. In this paper, Shenzhen city is taken as the study area. We use Mann-Kendall trend test method, wavelet analysis method and R/S method to explore the trend, cycle characteristics and persistence of annual rainfall, number of rainfall days and daily maximum rainfall in different areas of Shenzhen. The results show that the overall trend of annual rainfall in Shenzhen is not significant, and the spatial distribution of annual rainfall in the city will gradually form a decreasing pattern from east to west. The number of rainfall days in Shenzhen do not changed significantly with a variation of $2.7\sim 6.1$ d/10a, and the future the number of rainfall days may form a spatial distribution of more in the southeast and less in the northwest. The daily maximum rainfall variation in Shenzhen is $5.4\sim 12.2$ mm/10a. The future spatial distribution of daily maximum rainfall will maintain the situation of more in the southeast and less in the northwest, but the difference between the daily maximum rainfall in Dapeng and other areas will continue to become larger.

Author Keywords: Spatial and Temporal Distribution of Rainfall

articleTitle: Dynamic optimization of high-speed railway structure based on Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The coupling dynamics method is mainly used in the study of high-speed railway dynamics in China. At present, most of the research on vehicle dynamics only focuses on the analysis of single track parameters, and does not consider the influence of multi-objective parameters.
