Based on the vehicle-track coupling dynamics theory, the vertical dynamics model of vehicle-track structure is established by numerical analysis method to study the key parameter values of vehicle-track structure system. The influence of fastener stiffness, track bed stiffness and track bed thickness on the overall dynamic response of the system was analyzed under the condition of considering long-wave irregularity, and the genetic algorithm Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-ii was used to optimize the parameters. The optimization results showed that: The change of fastener stiffness Kr, track bed stiffness $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{b}}$ and track bed thickness $\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{b}}$ has a great influence on the acceleration response of ballast bed and sleeper and rail. It has a good effect on reducing rail fatigue damage, sleeper damage and ballastly ballastation. The reasonable range of fastener stiffness is $55\sim 80\mathrm{M}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$. The range of track bed stiffness is $280\sim 300\mathrm{M}\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$. The track bed thickness should be between $0.17\sim.23\mathrm{m}$.

articleTitle: Cause discussion and Stability Evaluation of the Accumulation body near the Dam of a hydropower station
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Between the upper dam site and the middle dam site of the planned a hydropower station, there is a large near-dam accumulation body. Whether the hydropower station can be approved by the state depends on whether the accumulation body is stable. Through field surveys and on-site geological exploration and other means, the development characteristics and material composition of the deposits near the dam of a hydropower station were revealed and it is estimated that the volume of the accumulation body is about $7200 \times 10^{4} {\mathrm {m}}^{3}$. It is judged that it is a large accumulation body composed of Quaternary collapse deposits and multi-periodic glacier (water) terminal or lateral moraine deposits. Because the accumulation body is located between the upper dam site and the middle dam site of the planned hydropower station, the stability of the accumulation body has attracted much attention. The stability of the accumulation was evaluated by a combination of qualitative and quantitative methods, and It was concluded that although there are blocks with poor local stability in the front edge of the accumulation body, due to the support and anti-slip effect of the bedrock pedestal under the accumulation body, the overall stability of the accumulation body is relatively good, After the water storage, the possibility of overall instability of the accumulation body is unlikely, and it has little impact on the planned hydropower station. The research results can provide references for the origin and stability evaluation of the corresponding accumulation body in southeastern Tibet.

articleTitle: Key Issues of Dual Prevention Mechanism Informatization in the Application of Water Resources and Hydropower Engineering
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: This paper studies several connotations of the dual prevention mechanism based on the actual informatization application in water conservancy and hydropower projects. Relevant solutions for informatization are proposed to provide references for the implementation of dual prevention mechanism informatization. Aiming at the problems that cannot be related to risk control and hidden hazard investigation and governance in the dual prevention mechanism, the risk identification library is established, with the risk identification content as the smallest management unit, to realize the internal correlation between risks and hidden hazards. An evaluation model is introduced to quantify risk evaluation indicators. For the problems that the dual prevention mechanism is difficult to implement and cannot be integrated with management, the effective implementation of dual control is facilitated by decomposing the content of control and controlling personnel behavior through informational means, and recording and implementing the process into the evaluation model. At the same time, for the self-assessment of risk management and control, a quantifiable and operable dynamic evaluation mechanism is introduced, and the relationship between risks and hidden hazards can be combined to further assist the dual prevention mechanism to play a role in the risk management and control of enterprises.

articleTitle: Influence of Automatic Detection on the Dynamic Response of the Large Diameter Bored Pile
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Information is the foundation of smart water conservancy, and we must attach great importance to the collection, monitoring and analysis of information; knowledge is the core of smart water conservancy, and new information technology must be applied to strengthen information mining, extraction and knowledge accumulation. The influence of automatic detection on the dynamic response of the large diameter bored pile is analyzed in this study. First, the sediment is considered as a fictitious soil pile and the Rayleigh-Love rod theory is introduced to establish the longitudinal dynamic governing equations for the pile and the fictitious soil pile to approximately consider the three-dimensional effect of the pile. Then, the dynamic governing equation for the surrounding soil is built based on the three-dimensional axisymmetric model. By means of Laplace transform, impedance function recursion and inverse Fourier transform, the dynamic governing equations for the soil-pile system are solved to derive the solution for dynamic response of the pile in the frequency and time domain. Based on the established solution, parameter sensitivity analysis is carried out to portray the three-dimensional effect of the large diameter bored pile and the influence of the thickness, density and longitudinal wave velocity of the sediment on the dynamic response of the pile. Finally, the reliability of the proposed solution is verified by comparing with the measured result.

articleTitle: Structural Safety Association Analysis for Operating Tunnel based on FP-growth Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Based upon the monitoring data from shield tunnels of 6 subways in a city, the standardized structure safety data set containing 350,000 tunnel segment data is built. The tunnel segment deformation, soil property, buried depth and surrounding environment etc. are considered in the data set. With FP-growth algorithm, association analysis of the influence factors onto the tunnel structural safety is carried out. In view of the structural defects of tunnel segments, the lift degree is selected as the index to evaluate the influences of the convergent deformation of tunnel segments, operating years and soil characteristics on segment defects. Based on the quantitative association rules of convergent deformation of tunnel segments, the influence of the independent factor on the convergent deformation under different operating years is analyzed. The association analysis results can reflect the distribution and development law of segment disease and convergent deformation, which is assistive to the operation and maintenance of Metro tunnel.

articleTitle: Influence of Temperature Variations on Seepage Pressure of Sluice Foundation: A Reconsideration
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The “abnormal phenomenon” of the seepage pressure of the very slightly permeable clay sluice foundation has puzzled the engineering and academic circles for more than half a century. To explain this phenomenon scientifically, based on the monitoring data of the seepage pressure of the sluice foundation and the temperature of the foundation soil in recent one year. As well as the temperature control test of the sluice foundation soil, the THM coupling numerical analysis of Sanhe Sluice Project is carried out. The monitoring and numerical simulation results show that there is a positive correlation between the seepage pressure and the temperature, that is, the seepage pressure increases when the temperature rises, and decreases when the temperature drops. This “abnormal phenomenon” of seepage pressure is actually the external manifestation of shear shrinkage or dilatation caused by the decrease or increase of the effective stress intensity of the very slightly permeable clay foundation. At the same time, the rise and fall of temperature will also cause the uplift or settlement of the sluice floor. The calculation method of seepage pressure recommended by the current Design Specifications for Sluices” does not consider the influence of temperature variations on the seepage pressure of sluice foundation, but the seepage pressure has an important influence on the stability of the sluice chamber, which must be paid attention to.

articleTitle: Research progress on coupling effect of multi-ion ionic attack of concrete in the coastal area
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The corrosion on concrete from seawater has an ion coupling effect. This paper analyzed the results of two species ionic coupling attack, three species ionic coupling attack, and seawater attack, which obtained the following results: (1) The internal pores will be blocked by the attack products of $\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}$ and Mg<sup>2+</sup> in the early stage, which inhibits the transportation of $\mathrm{C}1^{-}$; the degradation of concrete will increase the transport speed of $\mathrm{C}1^{-}$. (2) Sulfate attack is influenced by cation type. Taking expansion rate as deterioration index, Na<inf>2</inf>So<inf>4</inf> and K<inf>2</inf>SO<inf>4</inf> have the highest attack speed and degree, while CaSO<inf>4</inf> has the lowest attack degree. Taking compressive strength as the deterioration index, the attack degree of MgSO<inf>4</inf> is the highest, and that of Na2SO<inf>4</inf> and K<inf>2</inf>SO<inf>4</inf> is the lowest. (3) Temperature will affect the deterioration degree of concrete, and the deterioration degree of concrete is more severe at low temperatures. $\mathrm{CO}_{3}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{C}1^{-}$ will aggravate the MgSO<inf>4</inf> attack at low temperature $(5^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$ but not affect the MgSO<inf>4</inf> attack at room temperature. (4) Due to the different transport rates of ions in concrete, the surface layer of concrete is divided into Mgrich zone, S-rich zone, and Cl-rich zone according to the rich elements.

articleTitle: Study on seismic resilience of urban power supply network based on functional analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Taking urban power supply network as the research object, this paper proposes a framework and method to evaluate the seismic resilience of power supply network considering the functional characteristics of power supply network. Based on the grid element vulnerability model, the framework uses Monte Carlo to simulate the network element failure induced by earthquake damage. The power flow model with functional characteristics is focused to analyze the post-earthquake performance response of the power supply network. The dynamic importance of the influence of earthquake failure units on network function determines the post-earthquake recovery sequence of power supply network units. The post-earthquake recovery process is considered to prioritize restoring power supply to associated nodes. It analyzes the influence of other lifeline networks on the post-earthquake recovery sequence of power supply networks.

articleTitle: Key Technology of Improvement on Shield Muck in Water Rich Boulder Stratum
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to reduce the adverse effects of shield construction in water rich boulder stratum and solve the problems such as large cutter head wear, sticking phenomenon and surface settlement during construction, the study of soil improvement technology during construction of the earth pressure balance (EPB) shield in the water rich boulder stratum with a particle size larger than 200mm is carried out, with Chengdu metro line 17 as the engineering background. The improvement characteristics of boulders are evaluated from three aspects including mobility, permeability and agitation resistance, and the idea of improvement on muck in water rich boulder stratum is developed, that is, the foam injection rate is about 45%, the water injection rate is about 5%, and the bentonite injection is about 2%. The results show that this technology can provide the best parameters for the EPB shield construction in water rich boulder stratum.

articleTitle: Experimental Study On Seismic Resistance Of PVA-FRCC Medium - Long Column With Reinforcement Under Low Cyclic Load
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to improve the deformation performance and damage tolerance of frame columns under seismic load and optimize the seismic performance of frame columns, using polyvinyl alcohol fiber reinforced cement-based composite (PVAFRCC) instead of ordinary concrete is one of the effective ways. At present, many scholars' research on the seismic performance of PVA-FRCC columns mainly focuses on short columns with high axial compression ratio or using PVA-FRCC instead of ordinary concrete in beam column joints. Based on this, considering the influence of axial compression ratio, shear span ratio and longitudinal reinforcement ratio on the seismic performance of PVA-FRCC medium-long columns, seven medium-long columns with fiber volume content of 1% were designed in this paper. Through quasi-static test, the crack development of the specimens under low cyclic loading was observed, and their hysteretic behavior, skeleton curve Degradation of energy dissipation capacity and bearing capacity. The test results showed that each medium-long column has good ductility bending failure, and the concrete protective layer does not fall off during failure. Increasing the axial compression ratio can improve the cracking load, yield load and peak load of PVA-FRCC columns, but the ductility and energy dissipation capacity are reduced. At the same time, it can reduce the number of cracks and limit the width of cracks; With the increase of shear span ratio, the bearing capacity of PVAFRCC columns decreases, but the deformation capacity and energy dissipation capacity are greatly improved; With the increase of reinforcement ratio, the bearing capacity, ductility and energy dissipation capacity of PVA-FRCC columns are improved, and the degradation rate of stiffness and bearing capacity is slowed down, which can effectively improve the seismic performance of members; The shear span ratio and axial compression ratio have a great influence on the seismic performance of FRCC columns.

articleTitle: Study on Residual Stress Analysis and Cold Bending Effect of Cold Formed Section Steel
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The residual stress of cold-formed section steel with strength of G420, G460 and G690 was tested after passing 10mm and 6mm; According to the rapid development of measurement economy and the continuous progress of engineering technology, steel structure buildings continue to emerge, and cold-formed steel has been widely used in these buildings and shows good mechanical properties. This paper mainly studies the distribution of residual stress in cold-formed steel. Firstly, the existing residual stress measurement methods are introduced and compared, Finally, the cutting method is used as the residual stress test method in this experiment; The average residual stress and bending residual stress distribution curve of cold-formed section steel are obtained by selecting the data with thickness of 1. Finally, combined with the theoretical analysis of the generation of cold-formed section steel residual stress, the distribution characteristics of cold-formed section steel residual stress, average residual stress and bending residual stress are summarized, and a simple distribution model is proposed. The research results will provide important basic data for the in-depth study of the design method of the cold-formed steel members.

articleTitle: Key design points and simulation analysis of pedestrian twice crossing based on detailed design concept
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In view of the low efficiency of pedestrian crossing and the obvious conflict with turning vehicles at large signal control intersections, this paper carries out an in-depth investigation on pedestrian crossing behavior habits and analyzes the problems existing in pedestrian crossing. Based on the detailed design concept, this paper summarizes and refines the main design points of pedestrian twice crossing, discusses focusing on the combination of pedestrian phase and motor vehicle phase, and the right-turn vehicle “starting late”; Finally, taking the typical four-phase cross intersection as an example, using VISSIM software, the simulation analysis of the two situation of the current and optimization intersection is carried out. The results show that the pedestrian delay is obviously reduced without a significant increase in vehicle delay. This paper also verifies the rationality and feasibility of the pedestrian twice crossing improvement scheme based on the detailed design concept.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Rescue Support System with the Digital Platform for Flood Prevention and Mitigation in Qiantang River Basin
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Through designing and implementing the rescue support system with the digital platform for flood prevention and mitigation in the Qiantang River basin, this paper proposes an auxiliary rescue support decision-making system based on one-key navigation and summarizes and refines the core technologies of related business digitization. The rescue support system effectively manages the material and team elements of the emergency rescue and organizes the relevant data to realize the unification of the data structure of the rescue process, furnishing an auxiliary decision-making system for the emergency rescue support and laying down a basis for mining the value of the rescue data at a later stage. The technical solutions described in this paper provide references for the construction of auxiliary rescue support decision-making systems in other regions related to flood mitigation and help expand the coverage of flood mitigation information.

articleTitle: The Influence of Tower-Bridge Connection on the Seismic Performance of the Intake Tower Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Connection ways of the intake tower and working bridge have an essential influence on the static and dynamic performance of the integral structure of intake tower. In this study, the Connection ways of fixed and movable hinge supports between the intake tower and the working bridge were simulated based on the constraint equation in ADINA. The influences of different tower-bridge Connection ways on the static and dynamic performance of the intake tower-hoist chamber-working bridge-foundation-reservoir water system were investigated. The results show that the combined Connection way of fixed and movable hinged supports (Connection way 1) is more suitable for the bottom and side Connections of the tower-bridge. The natural frequencies, static displacement and extreme values of vertical tensile normal stress of intake tower-hoist chamber system are not significantly affected by the tower-bridge Connection ways. Under the seismic action, compared with Connection way 1, the effects of the displacement and acceleration vertical to the main stream, stress and hydrodynamic pressure of the whole structure with Connection way 2 are insignificant. Compared to Connection way 1, the displacement and acceleration along the main stream of the hoist chamber with Connection way 3 are increased by 32.41% and 16.29%, respectively, and the vertical tensile as well as the compressive normal stress and the principal tensile and compressive stress of key points on the whole structure can be increased by 10.0%-34.0%, and the maximum hydrodynamic pressure in the middle upper part of the tower back can be reduced by more than 30%.

articleTitle: Assessment of Standard Syntaxis of Basin and Sub-basin Flood and Urban Drainage in Taihu Basin
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Based on the existing flood control projects under the current flood control and drainage standards of the Taihu Basin, sub-basin, and urban, a 50a return period design storm that is the most unfavorable condition for flood control in the basin is selected as the rainfall data and input into the hydrological and hydrodynamic model for simulation. The safety capacity (K) and safety coefficient (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>) are used to evaluate the standard syntaxis of basin and sub-basin flood and urban drainage in Taihu Basin The results show that the basin, sub-baisn flood control standards and urban drainage standards are deficient of standard syntaxis. The current flood control standards of basin can basically prevent the 50a return period flooding of basin, but the sub-baisn flood control standards and urban drainage standards are shortage. The contradiction of standard syntaxis of basin and sub-basin flood and urban drainage in the northern of the study area is more prominent than that in the southern. The urban drainage activities by polder areas have affected the flood discharge capacity of the channels of basin and sun-basin along the river, and further increased the pressure of the flood control regulation and storage of the Lake Tai. It is urgent to accelerate the construction of the key projects to improve the flood control standards in the northern of Taihu Basin.

articleTitle: Study on simulation method of prestressed anchor cable reinforcement for large toppling slopes
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The construction of prestressed anchor cables is an effective means to improve the stability of slopes. Revealing its reinforcement mechanism has important theoretical significance for guiding the design of slope supports. Based on the reinforcement characteristics, anchoring process and failure modes of prestressed anchor cables, this paper proposes a simulation method of the cables in combination with discrete elements. This approach can truly reflect the interaction between mortar, anchor cable and rock mass in the anchorage section, and it can also reflect the existence of anchor piers. Taking the left bank slope of Delsi Hydropower Station as a research object, and aiming at the deformation and failure characteristics of deep flexural toppling, the design principle of prestressed anchor cable reinforcement for large toppling masses is put forward. The stress of anchor cables and the deformation of the slope under the conditions of different support strength, reinforcement position and construction time are analyzed. The reinforcement effect of prestressed anchor cables and the influence on slope stability of each scheme are evaluated. Finally, for high rock slopes that are prone to toppling instability, prevention suggestions are provided during excavation and reinforcement.

articleTitle: Multi-station joint forecast model of water level in Hongze lake based on PSO-LightGBM
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: A multi-Station joint forecast model of water Level based on PSO-LightGBM is proposed to solve the problems of low prediction accuracy and short effective prediction period of traditional time series model and univariate time series model. The most relevant hydrological stations are found out by calculating the Pearson correlation coefficient between the water level of Hongze Lake and the water level of relevant hydrological stations. The PSO-LightGBM single variable water level prediction model of these relevant hydrological stations is established to predict the future water level of relevant hydrological stations. Together with the water level of Hongze Lake, it is used as the multivariable in the Hongze Lake water level prediction model. The multi-Station joint forecast model of water Level in Hongze Lake based on PSO-LightGBM is established to predict the water level sequence of the next ten days of Hongze Lake. The case study shows that: the model has higher prediction accuracy than univariate PSO-LightGBM, ARIMA and LSTM models.

Author Keywords: South to North Water Diversion Project

articleTitle: An adaptive local mesh refinement strategy in numerical manifold method
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The numerical manifold method (NMM) is a powerful numerical analysis method based on the partition of unity, which is very suitable for the simulation of jointed rock mass. In order to achieve high accuracy and efficiency in simulating problems with large stress gradient such as stress concentration area and crack tip, an adaptive local mesh refinement algorithm based on the analysis-suitable T-spline (AS T-spline) is proposed in this paper. Specifically, the AS T-spline is applied to locally refine the mathematical cover of NMM in such regions as crack tips where stress concentration exists. The basis function of the cubic AS T-spline is derived and used as the weight function in the NMM to conduct the local refinement for a feasible adaptive procedure. Several numerical examples are given to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Method in High Flood Risk Area of River Basin Based on Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The continuous and rapid development of industrialization and urbanization in the past 40 years has caused the urban and rural landuse based on natural ecosystem in the western region of the Taihu Lake Basin to face the problems of landuse scale reduction and spatial structure fragmentation, which has led to a serious reduction in stormwater regulation and storage capacity. Starting from the effects of flood disaster mitigation in the river basin, this paper introduces the theory of complex adaptive systems, natural-based solutions, combined with the theoretical connotation of sponge city planning and construction, constructs a theoretical model of flood disaster complex system, and further builds a disaster mitigation effect evaluation model for sponge city planning and construction; the 3S method is used to evaluate and visualize the indicators, and the artificial intelligence BP neural network method is used to calculate the disaster reduction effect level of 357 plots in Yixing City. The results show that the disaster mitigation level in the mountain forest area and central urban area in the south of Yixing City is high, and the level in the north is low. This shows that the natural ecological large sponge has an obvious effect on urban flood disaster mitigation; appropriate LID measures can effectively compensate for the fewer defects of the large sponge; complementary, the through river network can reduce the flood disaster to a certain extent.

articleTitle: Research on intelligent monitoring system of hydraulic engineering based on digital twin
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The internet of things technology has promoted the development of safety monitoring automation to intelligence, and digital twin will surely further promote safety monitoring from intelligence to a higher level of monitoring intelligence. By analyzing the definition of digital twin, model system and intelligent monitoring technology, intelligent monitoring management and intelligent monitoring service connotation, as well as the typical application scenarios of intelligent monitoring system functions, intelligent monitoring essentially fits into the lightweight digital twin system. From the perspective of dam operation safety monitoring, an intelligent monitoring system architecture based on digital twin is proposed to further broaden the application field of digital twin, which is beneficial to promote the digital management of dam operation safety in the whole life period. And when using multi-discipline enabling technology to build a multi-dimensional, all-element dam and intelligent monitoring system of basic digital twin, it is necessary to break through and study several key technical issues under the new mode of symbiosis based on physical and virtual systems.

articleTitle: New mesoporous activated carbon obtained from municipal sludge and mangosteen peel for Cu(II) removal
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: A new and useful municipal sewage sludge combined with magnetic mangosteen peel adsorbent (MSM) was obtained by one-step preparation and proposed for Cu(II) removal. The surface structure, composition and functional group of MSM were characterised using scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction and Fourier transform infrared spectrometry. The N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> adsorption/desorption isotherms manifested that MSM was a porous carbon-based material, with a total pore volume of 0.93 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>·g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. The adsorption kinetics could be fitted with the pseudo-second-order model for the adsorbent. The adsorption isotherm indicated that the MSM was suitable for the Langmuir model with a maximum adsorption capacity of 127.64 mg·g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. The reusability tests showed that the removal rate of Cu(II) was maintained at approximately 75% by the desorbed MSM sample until the third cycle. The price of the main chemical reagent required to prepare 1 kg of MSM was ${\$}$4.09. The advantages of high adsorption capacity and adsorption rate of MSM suggested that such adsorbent is an effective adsorbent for Cu(II) removal.

articleTitle: Influence analysis and safety assessment of vehicle bomb type on the dynamic response of curved bridge under bridge deck blast load : ——(I): Influence analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In this study, to determine the dynamic response and failure mode of curved girder bridge under bridge deck explosion loading, a four-span curved continuous box girder bridge in a ramp bridge was adopted as the engineering background. The finite element models of curved girder bridge, and air were built. The failure mechanism of curved girder bridge based on various car bombs was analyzed by using the fluid-structure interaction method and “three-stage method”. As revealed from the results, under the scaled distance less than 0.18 m$\cdot {\mathrm {kg}}^{(-1/3)}$, the total volume of failure elements is linearly related to the scaled distance; The failure modes of curved box girder bridge under the blast of various vehicles can fall to three types: explosive pit, explosive penetration, and explosive punching; different failure mode will be caused under the blast of different vehicle bomb.

articleTitle: Study on Drainage Scheme and Safety Assessment during Construction of Land Forming Project in the Coastal Estuary Area
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: According to the construction organization and drainage requirements of the land area formation project of Shenzhen Ocean New City, the flood control and drainage schemes of different stages during the construction period were formulated, and the drainage scheme design and flood control safety assessment were carried out during the construction period. Based on the technical route combined with field survey of drainage channel, prototype data analysis and numerical simulation, the hydrological and hydrodynamic boundary conditions are reasonably generalized. Moreover, a two-dimensional hydrodynamic mathematical model of the drainage scheme during the construction period is established for the calculation and analysis on the hydrodynamic parameters such as the river water level, flow velocity and flow field of river drainage system within and around the project area. Following with comprehensive analysis on influence of drainage scheme on flood discharge capacity of upstream and downstream rivers during construction period, the security and reliability for the drainage project were evaluated with quantitative analysis. Necessary preventive and remedial measures were proposed to reduce the adverse effect on flood control safety of drainage system. Research results show that technical guarantee of the drainage safety can be implemented during the construction period of the land area formation project in the coastal estuary area.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Characteristics and Attribution of Runoff in the Upper Reaches of Yongding River in Recent 60 Years
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: For the annual runoff of the representative stations in the upper reaches of Yongding River from 1956 to 2016, the sliding T-test method, the linear trend method, the M-K method, and the R/S method are used to analyze the characteristics of annual runoff. Then the contribution ratio of the climate change and human activities to runoff change is studied by using the elastic coefficient method based on Budyko framework. The results show that the abrupt change points of Cetian, Xiangshuibao and Guanting hydrological stations appeared in 1982, 1983 and 1983 respectively. The precipitation in the control basins presented downward trend which is not significant, while the potential evapotranspiration presented a significant and sustainable downward trend. The underlying surface and potential evapotranspiration contribute negatively to the runoff reduction, but the precipitation contributes positively to the runoff reduction. The contribution rates of climate change to the runoff reduction of Cetian, Xiangshuibao and Guanting control basins are 17.5%, 19.1% and 17.2% respectively, of which the contribution rates of precipitation change to the runoff reduction are 21.6%, 26.2% and 21.0% and the contribution rates of potential evapotranspiration to runoff reduction are -4.0%, -7.1%, -3.8% respectively. Meanwhile, the contribution rates of human activities to runoff reduction are 82.5%, 80.9% and 82.8%, of which the contribution rate of changes in the underlying surface to the reduction of runoff are 67.5%, 73.3%, 52.8% and the contribution rates of changes in social water consumption and other factors to the reduction of runoff are 15.0%, 7.6% 30.0%, respectively.

articleTitle: Design Method and Mechanical Analysis of Fabricated L-shaped Steel Lattice Columns
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The current prefabricated steel structure residences had the problems of complex structure and inflexible layout, which limited the development of prefabricated steel structure. In order to solve the problem of exposed columns in prefabricated steel structure residence, a new L-shaped Steel Lattice Column (L-SSLC) was proposed. A simplified formula for ultimate bearing capacity of L-SSLC was produced by double coefficient multiplication method. The nonlinear finite element analysis of L-SSLC was performed using ABAQUS software, in which the compression performance was analysed. Theoretical results calculated by simplified formula were compared to that of the finite element analysis. The results indicate that the stress at the connection between batten plates and steel pipes is relatively large. Compared to axial compression columns, eccentric compression columns have better ductility and lower bearing capacity. The simplified formula is feasible and the redundancy factor is 1.12-1.41.

articleTitle: Study on a long-term temperature stress of a low-heat cement concrete high arch dam
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The structure of high arch dams is complex and the overall stress level is high. Therefore, the temperature field and stress field of high arch dams have always been the focus of related research. This article starts with the monitoring data, combined with simulation calculation, to study the long-term temperature stress change law of the high arch dam with low-heat cement concrete in the whole dam. After calculation and analysis, the following conclusions are drawn: (1) The use of low-heat cement concrete significantly reduces the difficulty of temperature control, and the maximum temperature of the entire dam is controlled within 27°C; (2) The internal temperature of the low-heat cement concrete arch dam is relatively stable after the arch is sealed. 2-5 years after the arch is closed, the external environment temperature will increase periodically; (3) With the passage of time, the overall tensile stress of the arch dam gradually decreases, and the concrete tensile stress of the main body of the dam is within the range of the 2.0 safety curve during the whole life cycle. There is a certain safety margin. The selection of the new low-heat cement concrete can effectively reduce the difficulty of early maximum temperature control in the project, and the residual hydration heat release effect in the later period is weak. The long-term tensile stress of the concrete in the project is in a safer position, which can make the construction more difficult. The selection of materials for arch dam projects can be used for reference.

articleTitle: Hydraulic Characteristics of Eco-friendly Spillways Using Numerical Simulation
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: To evaluate the potential impact of the construction and operation of a spillway on its downstream fish habitat, taking a reservoir project as an example, this paper uses a three-dimensional hydrodynamic mathematical model to study the hydraulic characteristics such as discharge capacity, water surface profile, velocity distribution, pressure distribution and flip scour pit. The results show that the numerical calculation results are in good agreement with the model test. The discharge capacity of the spillway meets the design requirements. The discharge capacity of the three overflow surface holes is similar. The design of the sidewall of the spillway is reasonable and reliable. The pressure distribution of the bottom plate is reasonable. The flow velocity is symmetrically distributed as a whole, and the flow pattern is good. The water tongue flip distance maintains a certain safe distance to meet the safety requirements of fish habitat downstream. At the same time, it is suggested to take 8-11 m as the reference to the scour hole depth for the protection of downstream fish habitat during water jet.

articleTitle: The application of big data real-time stream processing technology in earthquake rapid report
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: This paper briefly introduced SeisFLINK, a concurrent big data real-time stream processing platform established based on Apache Kafka and Apache Flink according to the actual requirements of earthquake rapid report. By comparing the actual earthquake monitoring data with the monitoring data of SeisComP3 and CENC, this paper summarized the the advantages of earthquake monitoring and rapid report of this system.

articleTitle: Research on static load test results of compresive and tensile piles in soft soil
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to study the differences of vertical bearing capacity and load transfer mechanism of single pile under compressive and tensile conditions, compressive and tensile static load tests of bored piles were carried out on a pile foundation project in Shanghai. The results show that due to the partial enlarger of the tensile pile diameter during construction, the pile body cracks and soil shear failure occurs, causing the uplifting displacement to be too large and the bearing capacity has much less than the bearing capacity of compressive piles. The ratio of pile end resistance to pile top load of compressive pile is very small, which the maximum does not exceed 1.5%. Therefore, it is unreasonable to blindly increase the pile length to enter hard soil layer. The pile side friction of compressive piles tends to decrease along the depth direction, and the compressive piles present semi-spindle-shaped distribution law of “large middle and small ends”, so pile side grouting is often adopted in the middle and lower part of the pile section to increase its vertical carrying capacity.

articleTitle: Research on the Temperature Control and Crack Prevention of A one-hundred-meter-long Complex Slab Concrete under the Constraint of Diaphragm Wall
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Due to the uneven temporal and spatial distribution of the temperature field and structural constraints, large-volume concrete structures are prone to structural cracks that endanger the safety and durability of the project at an early age. Aiming at a one-hundred-meter-long complex slab concrete structure under the constraint of the diaphragm wall, the temperature field and stress field of the foundation mass concrete structure poured in winter are simulated and analyzed under various conditions during the construction period. The calculation results show that the slab concrete cannot meet the anti-cracking requirements only through temperature control measures. And the maximum tensile stress can be reduced to below the tensile strength only by comprehensive temperature control measures and structural optimization or temperature control measures and expansive agent measures. The two optimal conditions and measures tried in this research can provide reference for similar projects.

articleTitle: Slope Displacement Forecasting of the Substations Based on the Support Vector Machine and Environmental Factor
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The accurate forecasting of slope displacement is necessary for the safe construction and operation of substations. Through comprehensive analysis of slope displacement effect factors, a slope displacement forecasting method based on support vector machine (SVM) and rainfall is proposed. Firstly, the correlation between slope vertical displacement and rainfall is analyzed. Then, the forecasting model is built based on historical vertical displacement and rainfall, using SVM algorithm. The forecasting error of the proposed forecasting model is 0.93%, and the accuracy of the method is verified to be high. It is proved that the slope displacement forecasting model based on SVM and environmental factor is effective.

articleTitle: In-situ seepage deformation testing method for shear zones
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Seepage deformation and failure characteristics of the shear zone in the dam site area of the Guxian hydro-junction in the Yellow River were studied through in-situ and indoor seepage deformation tests. The test results are as follows: the shear zone permeability coefficient and the critical gradient were obtained. In terms of the overall failure degree of the shear band during the test, the osmotic failure degree of the cleavage zone (shear fracture zone) in the shear band is lower, and the osmotic failure degree of the argillization zone (muddled intercalation zone) is higher, which has a great influence on the overall structure of the shear zone. The test results can provide a strong basis for engineering design calculations. In addition, the shear zone permeability deformation process is divided into four stages, which can provide a reference for future studies on the permeability deformation of adverse geological bodies such as shear zones.

articleTitle: Mechanism Analysis of TETON Dam Failure
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: under the current codes of the TETON Dam, the conclusions are contrary to the facts. Cautioned engineers who simply comply with regulatory requirements by current codes would be calculated as a dam safety assurance, or the sole judge. Expounded review the TETON dam which has been crashed more than 35 years ago by using today’s ideas and skills is necessary. Combined with survey information, the 2D and 3D seepage result confirmed the main reasons for TETON dam failure are incorrect curtain design and contact zone’s treatment. Expounded review the hydraulic structure which has been crashed passed by using today’s ideas and skills is necessary.

articleTitle: Model tests of slope deformation mechanism under pulse-like waves
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: A test model with scale of 1:25 is designed and a monitoring system combining contact measurement and noncontact measurement is constructed. Shaking table tests under different amplitudes of the pulsed ground motions are carried out. The results show that the amplification effect first increases and then decreases with the amplitude of the pulsed wave increases. The deformation process of slope under the pulsed ground motion is as follows: settlement mainly occurs at the top of the slope, and sand in the upper part begins to slide towards the slope toe.

articleTitle: Research on Moment Amplitude Modulation Coefficient of Unbonded Prestressed Concrete Continuous Beam
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The research ideas of moment amplitude modulation coefficient of unbonded prestressed concrete (UPC) continuous beam is put forward. Through nonlinear finite element analysis of unbonded prestressed concrete continuous beam, two factors affecting moment amplitude modulation of equivalent plastic hinge length and section curvature ductility coefficient are analyzed in details. The calculation formulas of equivalent plastic hinge length, ductility coefficient of section curvature and amplitude modulation coefficient of bending moment are given and compared with experimental data. The results can be used as the basis for the plastic design of unbonded prestressed concrete beams.

articleTitle: Intelligent monitoring and disaster avoidance in the construction of steel frame reinforced concrete hybrid structure
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Due to the high strength of steel, hybrid structure can effectively reduce the column section and increase the building area, so it is widely used in super high-rise buildings. However, with the increase of the height of super high-rise building and the extension of construction period, the vertical deformation difference between frame column and core tube is becoming larger and larger, and its influence on the levelness of building structure roof and the additional stress in horizontal members is also becoming larger and larger. Therefore, this paper uses the finite element analysis software MIDAS Gen to carry out intelligent monitoring and disaster avoidance for the whole construction process of a super high-rise building, and mainly explains the modeling process, intelligent monitoring and result analysis.

Author Keywords: steel frame reinforced concrete hybrid structure

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Erosion of Segment Concrete under Bending Load, Sulfate and Chloride
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In this paper, the erosion test of segment concrete underthree working conditions of 5%Na2SO4+5%NaCl+0/0.3/0.5Pcr (Pcr is the ultimate bending load) is designed. Through ultrasonic velocity test, SO42- and Cl- concentration test, the influence of bending load on sound velocity change and SO42- and Cl- diffusion law is analyzed. The results show that with the increase of erosion period, the sound velocity increases first and then decreases, and the sulfate corrosion resistance increases first and then decreases. With the increase of bending load, the sound velocity decreases gradually, and the resistance to sulfate erosion weakens gradually. With the increase of bending load, the concentration of SO42- and Cl- in each erosion depth and erosion cycle increases, and the bending load accelerates the diffusion of SO42- and Cl- obviously. The concentration of SO42- and Cl- increases with the increase of erosion time, and decreases with the increase of erosion depth. The diffusion velocity in the shallow depth is obviously higher than that in the deep depth, and the diffusion depth of SO42- is obviously shallower than that of Cl-.

articleTitle: Change Pattern of Velocity of Intermediate Channel with Unsteady Flow Resulted by Ship Lock Discharge
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The velocity evolution process caused by the unsteady flow of lock discharge, where the key problem is the relationships between the hydraulic factors in the restricted middle navigable channel and the transformation of unsteady flow and the corresponding scales are investigated. Based on the restricted middle navigable channel of the Baise navigation project, the relationship between the unsteady flow discharge process of lock and the velocity evolution process in the restricted middle channel is studied through systematic experiments, and the conclusion is drawn as follows. The main reason caused the flow fluctuation is attributed to insufficient energy dissipation, the rapid increase of discharge during the lock discharge process, and the limited boundaries. By reducing the peak value of the time-discharge curve, the maximum velocity and maximum inverse velocity decrease in the upper restricted middle navigable channel. In the long restricted middle navigable channel, due to the energy consumption, the velocity fluctuation in the downstream is much smaller than that in the upstream, which still exists after the flow pattern reaches a steady state. This study can provide a theoretical basis for the middle channel layout design.

articleTitle: Study on mechanical response and disturbance control of shield underpass pre-reinforcement soil
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Based on the construction method of reserved underpass space for shield tunneling and Hangzhou Metro Line 7 under Qianjiang Century City construction project. A three-dimensional calculation model of soil reinforcement with reserved underpass space was established by using numerical simulation method, and the mechanical disturbance of soil around the tunnel during the shield tunneling process was analyzed. The results show that under the condition of local soil reinforcement, heave deformation exists in the strengthened area, resulting in a large relative displacement between the local strengthened area and surrounding soil. That results in stress concentration at the interface between the reinforcement area and the surrounding soil. The isolation and protection effect of the diaphragm wall and reducing pile on the soil is revealed by monitoring the displacement.

articleTitle: Research on Surface Deformation Control of Tunnel Construction Under-passing Petroleum Pipeline
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The intersection of new tunnels and existing structures is a common problem during tunnel construction. Therefore, how to ensure the structural safety of existing structures during the excavation of new tunnels is a difficulty in construction. This paper takes the Kelewan loess tunnel of the Mianxi Expressway as the research background, and uses numerical simulation methods to study the surface deformation control of the shallow-buried loess tunnel underneath the oil pipeline; Comparative analysis shows that the reasonable length of the leading small conduit is 4.5m; in order to reduce the impact of tunnel construction on the existing oil pipeline, vertical grouting pre-reinforcement is carried out on the ground around the oil pipeline. When different grouting widths and depths are used, The maximum settlement value of the petroleum pipeline is compared and analyzed. It is recommended that the grouting width is 3.05m and the grouting depth is 4.5m. In order to obtain the optimal construction parameters, it will provide a reference for similar projects in the future.

articleTitle: Effect of the construction sequence of bridge approach on piled abutments in soft silty clay
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: A series of well-established 3-D numerical analyses based on centrifuge tests were conducted to examine the effect of the construction sequence on a piled abutment over soft ground. Two extreme construction sequences were studied: (i) a sequence involving installing the piled abutment until its settlement is totally stable, then followed by constructing the approach embankment (i.e., test X); (ii) a sequence involving installing the piled bridge abutment and constructing the approach embankment simultaneously (i.e., test T). Results indicated that owing to more adequate consolidation process of soft soil after the abutment installation for test X, the normal contact pressure in magnitude was larger than that for test T along the entire pile shaft. By comparison between tests T and X, the rotation direction of the abutment wall is closely associated with the moment equilibrium dominated by earth pressures against the abutment wall and normal contact pressures resisted on the piles. The construction sequence imposed a limited influence on the maximum bending moments, accounting for about 55% of the ultimate bending moment capacity of the pile in both tests T and X.

articleTitle: Field prototype experiment of rockfill temperature before SCC filling for rock-filled concrete dam
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The estimation of the rockfill temperature in practical engineering is of great significance to calculate the temperature rise of rock-filled concrete. Through the field prototype experiments of monitoring the rockfill temperature, the non-uniform temperature field along with the seasonal distribution was analyzed by qualitative and quantitative approaches. When the rockfill in a lift surface is treated as an equivalent ‘rock’ with porous structure, some results were manifested that: (1) The temperature of the exposed rockfill is more susceptible to the air (solar radiation and convection etc.), which results in the heterogeneity and seasonal variability; (2) The estimation of the rockfill temperature can be roughly conducted by its relationship with the air temperature. (3) The influence of the air temperature on the rockfill is nearly linear with the depth, and the thermal conductivity can be estimated for the future numerical simulations. Further work is in process for the mechanism of heat conduction between rockfill and SCC.

articleTitle: Seismic ground motion parameters for automatic seismic trip system of nuclear power plants
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: After the Fukushima accident in Japan, the nuclear safety regulatory authorities of South Korea and other countries have required the installation of automatic seismic trip system (ASTS). In 2019, the National Nuclear Safety Administration issued the Seismic Design and Evaluation of NPPs (HAD102/022019), which specifies the role of seismic instruments in nuclear power plants (NPPs), including the role of ASTS. At the same time, it also puts forward relevant requirements on whether to install the ASTS. In 2019, China revised and issued Code for seismic design of nuclear power plants (GB 50267-2019), the seismic alarm index should be fully demonstrated. According to the investigation and study of the nuclear safety regulations and standards, and combining with the seismic level of NPPs site in China, this paper puts forward some suggestions on whether to set ASTS and the selection of ground motion parameters of ASTS.

articleTitle: Research on Integrated 3D Platform of Rock Engineering Analysis and Design
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The most direct impact is that it is difficult to carry out excavation, calculation, support and other geotechnical engineering design work directly based on the three-dimensional geological model according to the building layout requirements. The internal reason is that the geotechnical engineering design work involves both irregular geological objects and regular structural objects The description of the two objects involves different basic theories and algorithms, computer graphics technology and user’s operating habits, and there are natural “technical barriers”. The research and development of the integrated three-dimensional system of geotechnical engineering analysis and design starts from the bottom technology. It adopts two kinds of algorithm theory of “discrete” and “continuous”, two kinds of program data structure of nonparametric and parametric, “double engine” technology of two operation modes of “uncertainty” and “determination”, and embeds mechanical calculation engine to carry out mechanical analysis and calculation for geological body structure, which meets the requirements of rock mass. The design of soil engineering needs, and fundamentally solves the interface problem of Geology and structure.

articleTitle: Fast Simulation of Attenuation Relations of Ground Motion Parameters and Seismic Intensity Map in Shandong and Adjacent Areas
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The observed data of 151 sets of strong motion seismographs and 126 seismic equipment in Shandong Province were used. According to the site conditions, Shandong and its adjacent areas were divided into bedrock exposed areas and soil covered areas. The attenuation characteristic relations between ground motion parameters-peak velocity and peak acceleration-in Shandong and adjacent areas were studied through least squares fitting, and the corresponding relational expressions were given. In case of a strong motion, the earthquake early warning system could realize the fast estimation of earthquake magnitude using the data in the first 3s. Moreover, the peak acceleration and peak velocity values could be rapidly obtained according to the abovementioned attenuation characteristic relations. Secondly, the seismic intensity could be estimated fast through the calculation method of seismic intensity in the instrument based on the technical standard systems related to seismic intensity rapid reporting and early warning. Moreover, the seismic intensity distribution map could be rapidly simulated by introducing the thought of triangular mesh generation.

articleTitle: Water Quality Simulation and Improvement Under the Combined Scheduling of Sluice Gates and Pumps in the Lixia River Area
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The Lixia River area in Jiangsu Province is a typical plain river network area in the lower reaches of the Jianghuai Plain. The water system in the area is characterized by strong artificial control, close upstream and downstream connections, and slow flow of water. In this study, we use the coupled model of hydrology, hydrodynamics and water quality of the river network in the Lixia River area to simulate the changes of water quality and hydrodynamic conditions of the regional river network under different joint scheduling schemes, and analyze the effect of different schemes on improving the regional water environment. Considering the different conditions of diversion control, drainage control, starting time and river section connectivity, a total of five water transfer schemes were set up to simulate and analyze the effect of water environment improvement during the non-flood season. Through the analysis of regional water quality representative sites, the effect of water transfer on the improvement of the water environment in different areas of the hinterland is different, with a significant effect in the south of the study area, most of the indicators of water quality after the transfer of water to reach the national water quality standard and significantly better than the current water quality as well as the results in the middle area. The reduction of COD, BOD5 organic pollutant concentration in the north of the study area has a certain role, but does not have the improvement of N, P nutrient pollution function. The region-wide water transfer simulation experiments can provide technical support for the attempt of optimal scheduling of water environment under the watershed management system, taking the watershed as a unit and breaking the administrative division.

Author Keywords: water quantity and quality coupling model

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis of Seismic Performance of Duplex Concrete Filled Steel Tubular Column and Steel Beam Spatial Joint
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: To study the influence of the cutting depth of the beam flange on the seismic performance of the spatial joints between the duplex concrete-filled steel tubular column and H-shaped steel beam, six finite element models were established using ABAQUS finite element software, and low-cycle reciprocating loads were applied to the beam ends of the joint model. The results show that the cutting depth of the steel beam flange has a greater impact on the seismic resistance of the spatial joint between the duplex concrete-filled steel tubular column and the steel beam. With the increase of the cutting depth, the energy dissipation capacity of the joint first increases and then decreases, and the ductility of the joint is improved, but the stiffness and limit bearing capacity of the joint has decreased. Especially when the cutting depth is too large, the web in the weakened area of the H-shaped steel beam is prone to buckling instability.

articleTitle: Finite Element Simulation of Seismic Behavior of Shear Wall with High Strength Steel Bar
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The finite element simulation of the shear wall model with end column and end column with high strength steel bar was carried out under low cyclic reversed loading test. Taking the strength of longitudinal steel bar and stirrup as the main parameters, the shear wall models under four working conditions were established, which were end column with ordinary steel bar, end column with high strength stirrup and ordinary longitudinal steel bar, end column with high strength longitudinal steel bar and ordinary stirrup, and end column with high strength stirrup and high strength longitudinal steel bar. The finite element software ABAQUS was used to simulate the loading of each shear wall model, and the seismic performance indexes such as hysteresis curve, skeleton curve, stiffness degradation curve, ductility coefficient and energy dissipation capacity were extracted and analyzed. The results show that when the longitudinal steel bar of the end column is configured with high-strength steel bar; the seismic bearing capacity increases significantly, but the ductility decreases.

articleTitle: The Explicit Finite Element Analysis of the Concrete Arch Dams from Local Damage to Whole Failure
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In this paper, the failure process of concrete arch dam is the focus of research. Based on the quasi-static solution technique, the explicit analysis method is used to study the failure process of 78m high concrete double-curve arch dam under the condition of homogeneous dam foundation. The whole process of plastic failure of the concrete arch dam with homogeneous foundation in the process of overload from local damage to whole failure is studied. The numerical simulation results show that under the same load case, the calculation results of explicit analysis and implicit analysis are basically the same. The implicit analysis does not converge when the overloaded factor is 1.64, and the explicit analysis method based on the quasi-static solution technique can simulate the failure process of the arch dam more complete. When the overloaded factor reaches 6.0, the plastic failure zone of the dam body is connected, and the arch dam structure fails.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization Methods of Flood Dispatching Scheme Based on Decision Trees
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In river basin flood control, a huge database has been formed by the accumulation of massive data and dispatching information feedbacks. The potential relations or modes between the data can be fully mined using the decision tree algorithm. Therefore, the decision tree algorithm was used in this paper to preliminarily discuss and sufficiently mine the potential relations or modes through river basin flood control data to guide the reservoir scheduling.

articleTitle: Effect of tip clearance on gas phase distribution of a gas-liquid two-phase pump
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In this paper, the effects of tip clearance on the external characteristics, internal flow field, load distribution and gas phase distribution of gas-liquid two-phase three-stage mixed transport pump under different void fraction are studied based on numerical simulation. It is verified that the numerical simulation is reliable by comparing with the experiment. The main results show that with the increase of blade tip clearance, the head and efficiency of mixed transport pump show a downward trend; Reasonable tip clearance can effectively improve the gas phase distribution in the impeller. For the mixed pump studied in this article, when the tip clearance is less than 0.28%D (impeller diameter), the gas distribution in the impeller becomes more uniform as the clearance value increases.

articleTitle: Analysis of Heightened Dam Working Behavior During Impoundment Process
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In the second half of 2017, the Danjiangkou Reservoir carried out an experimental impoundment. Based on this impoundment, the three-dimensional finite element simulation technology is applied to simulate the temperature and stress distribution during the whole process from concrete placement to trial impoundment completion. The working behavior of the dam including change of temperature, stress, deformation and the open degree of joint surface during the impoundment process is emphatically analyzed and compared with the measured results. The results show that the whole dam section deforms downstream under the combined effect of the water rising and temperature decreasing during the impoundment process. The calculated results are consistent with the measured values. The temperature and stress in the dam body are not affected obviously during the impoundment process, but the surface temperature drops obviously, stress increases significantly on the surface and downstream slopes. The vertical joint faces of dam tend to be closed.

articleTitle: Simplified Analysis on the Generation Process of Horizontal Cracks in the Core Wall of a Core Dam Considering the Arching Effect
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The dam shell has certain restriction on the core wall due to settlement differences between the dam shell and the core wall. This paper analyzes the evolution process of the soil layer in the core wall from equilibrium state to non-equilibrium state and then to a new equilibrium state during settlement by establishing a generalized model of the arching effect during core dam settlement. It also studies and analyzes the adaptive process of core wall soil layer gap generation, and then, considers the impact from the upstream water pressure after impoundment, studies and analyzes the generating process of hydraulic fracture, and forms a simplified generalized model that can be used to determine the rough location and possibility of hydraulic fracture quickly. Furthermore, it verifies the feasibility of the method by comparing monitoring data and numerical analysis results. In addition, it provides certain basis for important control points during dam body filling, and it can be applied to searching key target points in the operation period and gradual determination of generation possibility and locations of horizontal cracks, providing a quick determination method for the study of core wall hydraulic fracture as well as project monitoring and analysis.

articleTitle: Study on the design of similar model test of parallel rectangular pipe jacking construction
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to study the interaction of parallel rectangular pipe jacking construction and its influence on surrounding strata, a similar model test design of parallel rectangular pipe jacking construction was carried out based on an engineering project. The main factors affecting the mechanical properties of rectangular pipe jacking construction process were analyzed, and the basic physical quantities were selected to deduce the similarity between model and prototype. Based on the similarity theory, the similar relations among the various physical quantities are analyzed through dimensional analysis method, the similarity ratio relationship suitable for pipe jacking construction model is obtained. Rectangular pipe jacking is realized by meeting geometric and elastic modulus similarity ratio, and model soil is realized by satisfying cohesion and elastic modulus similarity ratio. The data measurement and acquisition scheme of model test was designed, and the surface settlement, earth pressure and pipe jacking strain can be measured and analyzed. The key points in the model test process are pointed out through the simulation of the test process. The experimental design can meet the test requirements and achieve the test goal of parallel rectangular pipe jacking construction.

articleTitle: Experimental study on damage law of fully graded concrete under tension compression cyclic load
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Considering the reciprocating action of seismic load and the high compressive stress level of high arch dam, the damage law of fully graded concrete under tension compression cyclic load is studied. Based on 15MN large-scale dynamic material testing machine and specially designed linking device, the complete stress-strain curve of full graded concrete under cyclic load is obtained by means of high-precision axial extensometer and VIC-3D. The test data show that even at the medium and low pressure stress level, the full graded concrete will produce a certain amount of residual deformation, and has a good linear relationship with the pressure. Because the difference of ultimate strain between tension and compression of concrete is about 10 times, the compressive residual has great influence on the ultimate tensile strain. Ignoring the residual deformation under high pressure will overestimate the tensile strength of fully graded concrete, which is unsafe. Based on the stress-strain curve of tensile damage of fully graded concrete, it can be seen that the elastic modulus of fully graded concrete cannot be recovered immediately after tension compression conversion, but there is an obvious transition zone. The calculation results of the model ignoring the transition zone are unsafe.

articleTitle: Influence of the Warning Area Division on the Effect of the Propagation of Local Undamped Motion (PLUM) Method
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: It is possible to obtain a detailed estimates of the expected vibration by dividing the early warning area, to achieve an optimized early warning effect. This paper studies the influence of the warning area division on the warning effect of the the Propagation of Local Undamped Motion (PLUM) method. Japan is divided into grids with side lengths ranging from 30 km to 120 km, and each grid is considered an early warning area. Using the data recorded by the National Research Institute for Earth Science and Disaster Resilience (NIED), we studied the effects of different grid sizes on PLUM warnings by simulating the "311 earthquake" in Japan. The simulation results obtained with the grid divisions are compared with the simulation results obtained using predefined warning areas, and the influence and applicability of the warning area division method on the warning effect are analyzed. The calculation results show that an increased grid size leads to an expanded warning range, but at the same time, unnecessary warnings are sent to some areas.
