Under the conditions of the "311 earthquake" in Japan, the prediction scores and precision of the 60 km and 70 km grid are higher, and the mean warning times is longer than those of other grid sizes; the overall warning results of these grids are the closest to those obtained with the predefined warning areas in Japan.

Author Keywords: the Propagation of Local Undamped Motion (PLUM) method

articleTitle: Evaluation of resilience of bridge engineering system under earthquake disaster
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to ensure the safety of bridge construction and improve the anti-seismic defense capability of bridge construction, based on the concept and characteristics of toughness theory, the toughness evaluation of the bridge is carried out. In this paper, starting from the three attributes of disturbance force, absorption force and resilience, considering the characteristics of bridge construction, safety management, emergency measures, etc., a bridge seismic safety and toughness evaluation index system containing 22 indicators is determined. Take G1-Entropy Weight Method (EW) as the composite weight and construct a single index measurement function. Finally, the set pair analysis is introduced into the unascertained measure theory. Use this model to determine the toughness grade of the bridge and verify the rationality and feasibility of the model through examples. Providing a new way of thinking for bridge seismic toughness assessment.

articleTitle: Influence of foundation pit excavation on deformation of subway tunnel below
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the change of stress field caused by the excavation of a foundation pit in Zhengzhou drives the vertical and horizontal displacement and deformation of the subway tunnel which has been put into operation. In this paper, ABAQUS finite element software is used to conduct three-dimensional numerical simulation of foundation pit excavation, and the influence of the same foundation pit area but different length and width and the distance between the tunnel and the center of the foundation pit on the tunnel is discussed, and the size of the bending moment of the single tunnel under the foundation pit is analyzed during the excavation process. The results show that the excavation of the pit with four equal sides has the greatest effect on the vertical displacement of the tunnel below, which increases by 19.90% compared to the original pit shape displacement, and the vertical displacement of the tunnel increases by 14.58% compared to the original pit for the excavation of the pit with long sides parallel to the tunnel. When the horizontal distance of the tunnel from the center of the pit increases in sequence, the vertical displacement of the top of the tunnel will gradually decrease, and when the horizontal distance is 28m, the vertical displacement of the tunnel is 6.56mm. During the excavation of the pit, a pressure and tension area will appear in the tunnel section near the bottom of the enclosure structure, and this area will approach the center of the pit as the excavation depth deepens. The research results provide reference significance to the protection of the subway tunnel below the foundation pit during the excavation of the foundation pit under the geological conditions in Zhengzhou area, and accumulate experience for the construction of the project around the tunnel in Zhengzhou are

articleTitle: High-quality construction technology of steel structure of Hubei Olympic Sports Center Complex
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The modern gymnasium adopts complex steel structure design, and the originality of steel structure design presents new challenges to the construction technology. At present, it is urgent to seek solutions by combining theory with concrete projects. Based on the comprehensive gymnasium project of Hubei Olympic Sports Center Complex, this paper discusses and summarizes the engineering technical route that emphasizes both theory and practice. On this basis, six key technologies have been innovated, including efficient and comprehensive application of BIM associated with all professional construction, design and construction of anchor type fine rolled rebar self-locking reaming anchor rod in foundation construction, construction of high-precision embedded parts of octave prism cap structure in civil steel structure construction. Some key problems in construction and corresponding treatment measures, including the design of anti-floating anchor bolt and the design of aluminum steel keel, are emphatically expounded. It is expected to provide reference for the construction scheme of various steel structures.

articleTitle: Influence of floor layout on seismic performance of Frame-shear wall structure
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to study the influence of floor layout on the seismic performance of high-rise frame shear wall structure, taking the 12 storey reinforced concrete frame shear wall structure as an example, the calculation model is established by using ANSYS finite element software, and the structure under the action of earthquake is calculated and analyzed. The modal characteristics, natural frequency and maximum displacement, inter-story displacement angle and Mises equivalent stress distribution law of the structure under different floor layout schemes are obtained. The results show that the layout of 150mm-thick floor slabs for 1-6 floors and 120mm-thick floor slabs for 712 floors is the most beneficial to the overall lateral stiffness of the structure. The most dangerous section of the structure under the action of an earthquake is located at the bottom of the underlying shear wall. The calculations are carried out in accordance with the current concrete structure design code GBJ50010-2010 and the building seismic design code GB50011-2010.

articleTitle: Measured Results and Simulation Analysis of Transient Process of Pumped Storage Unit in XianJu
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The simulation of hydraulic transition process of pumped storage power station is the premise to guide the design and optimization of water conveyance system and ensure the safe and stable operation of the system. In this paper, the mathematical model of hydraulic transition process simulation calculation of Xianju pumped storage power station is established. Taking the guide vane opening and closing law actually used in Xianju pumped storage power station as the boundary, the field measured data and numerical simulation calculation results of single machine load rejection and single machine pumping outage of the power station are compared and analyzed respectively. The two are in good agreement, which verifies the accuracy of numerical simulation. Based on the measured results and numerical simulation calculation results of single machine, a correction method is put forward according to the most unfavorable correction principle, so as to predict the extreme values of the parameters under extreme working conditions such as double machine load rejection and double machine pumping outage. The correction method provides a theoretical basis for the long-term and safe operation of the power station, and it has important guiding significance for the inversion calculation and extreme value prediction of the hydraulic transition process of similar projects.

articleTitle: Study on the Recovery Performance of RC Beams Reinforced by Shape Memory Alloy Wire
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Using the superelasticity and one-way memory function of shape memory alloy SMA to generate greater driving force, a smart concrete beam was developed. Through experiments, the bending resistance and deformation laws of smart concrete beams with shape memory alloy wires are studied, and the optimal solution of composite SMA wires in the mechanical properties of the beams is found. The test results show that laying a one-way memory composite super-elastic shape memory alloy wire on the bottom of the RC beam can effectively improve the deformation ability of the test beam, and the content of the memory wire and the super-elastic wire are different, and their deformation laws and flexural properties are also different.% Memory wire compound 50% super elastic wire has the best repair effect when the damage degree is 70%.

articleTitle: High-temperature Resistance of Lateritic Soil-based Geopolymer Concrete in Comparison with Portland Cement
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The production of Portland cement pollutes the environment and waste energy, which does not meet the requires of the eco-friendly development. This study aims to investigate the resistance of lateritic soil-based geopolymer concrete at elevated temperatures $(20 \sim 1000^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$) to expand the application range. This study reported both fresh properties (slump and porosity) as well as high temperature performance (physical appearance, compressive strength development, and mass loss) of geopolymer (GPC) or Portland cement concrete (PCC) with various mixtures. The experimental results revealed that the superplasticizer could improve the fresh properties of PCC, and the slump value and porosity reached 100mm and 11.57%, two types of GPC presented worse porosity of more than 18%. Besides, GPC presented acceptable strength/mass retention together with physical appearance after exposed to high-temperature compared to PCC, especially at temperatures of over 500°C.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Moisture Changes in Shallow Unsaturated Loess under Atmospheric Action and its Influencing Factors
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Moisture variations in shallow loess soils induce diseases like sinking and cracking in road foundations and pavements, whereas temperature and stress changes in shallow loess soils are determined by moisture changes and influencing variables. To study the moisture change pattern of shallow unsaturated loess in semi-arid northwest China under atmospheric action. Model experiments of remolded loess were conducted, with remolded soil samples being measured under various starting circumstances. The findings of the experiments show that atmospheric activity has less impact on internal moisture changes in soils with a high dry density. The internal moisture migration of the soil sample is affected by heat transfer under atmospheric action at the same depth. The interior pores of the soil progressively link along the depth direction as a result of atmospheric action, and the water gradually distributes higher, enabling leftover water to evaporate. The longer the atmospheric action lasts, the longer the impact of moisture change in soils with high starting volume water content lasts. Moreover, in terms of moisture fluctuation at the subgrade, soils with an initial volume moisture content of less than 23% are essentially unaffected by atmospheric activity.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation study on settlement disease of pile foundations in frozen soil area treated by freezing method
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: During the operation period of Qinghai Tibet railway, permafrost degradation induced the decrease in the bearing capacity of bridge pile foundation and harmful settlement deformation for piles happened partially in permafrost regions, and even serious settlement deformation came into being in a short time, which results in the displacement and damage of bridge superstructure and seriously affects the normal operation of the engineering. Until now, there is a lack of rapid repair technology for bridge pile foundation settlement damage in permafrost regions. In this paper, artificial freezing technology was proposed to deal with the settlement damage of piles in permafrost area. In this paper, artificial freezing technology was proposed to deal with the settlement damage of piles in permafrost area. The feasibility and control effect are analyzed by using the three-dimensional numerical simulation model of freezing pipe pile foundation, and the influence of freezing parameters on freezing effect is studied. The results show that the artificial freezing method can quickly reduce the permafrost temperature around the pile and has a good cooling effect on the temperature field of the pile base. The distance between the freezing pipe and the pile and the cold liquid temperature have the most significant effect on the freezing effect. Therefore, in the treatment of pile foundation diseases by artificial freezing, the distance from freezing pipe to pile and cold liquid temperature should be considered as the main technical focus.

articleTitle: Study on the force transfer characteristics of the transverse joints of high arch dams considering the spherical keyway
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to reduce temperature stress, transverse joints are often used to divide large concrete structures into several pieces. In order to improve the structural integrity, keyways are often provided on the joint surface to compensate for the enhancement of the joint surface shear resistance and improve the structural integrity. In the design of high arch dams, the application of spherical keyways on the transverse joints are more and more widespread. Due to the huge workload of simulating the spherical keyway densely distributed on the joint surface, there are few related results that accurately simulate the transverse joint keyway and truly reflect the force transmission characteristics of the keyway of high arch dams during earthquakes. In order to study the force transmission characteristics of the spherical keyway in the high arch dam during the seismic process, this paper proposes a parametric simulation modeling method for the high arch dam considering the spherical keyway of the transverse joint, and establishes the foundation-water-dam dynamics considering the spherical keyway. The calculation model uses high-performance parallel computing technology for calculation and analysis. The relationship between the high stress area of the keyway surface and the opening of the transverse joint, and the force transmission characteristics of the location of the maximum shear stress in the high arch dam during a strong earthquake are studied in detail.

articleTitle: Effect of double track tunnel with small distance on existing tunnel deformation
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: MIDSA/ GTS software is used to simulate the double track parallel shield construction. The influence of double track shield construction on the existing tunnel under different small clear distance is studied, and the displacement and plastic zone development law of the existing tunnel are summarized. The analysis shows that the subsequent shield excavation will cause the clearance expansion and vault subsidence of the existing tunnel, and the uplift deformation of the inverted arch and the plastic zone of the surrounding rock of the tunnel will further become larger. When the clear distance is only 0. 8 times the tunnel diameter, reinforcement measures need to be taken.

articleTitle: Study on the dynamic response of the powerhouse under the vibration load of the Hydropower Station
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The vibration problem of hydro-turbine generator sets is very complicated. There are examples at home and abroad that the vibration of the generator sets causes the vibration of the plant structure, and even causes the structural damage to affect the normal operation of the power station. The Hydropower Station is a second-class (2) type project. In order to study the dynamic response of the plant under the vibration load of the unit, the finite element dynamic time history method is adopted, and the vibration loads are assumed to be simple harmonic loads. The dynamic response of the plant under the four working conditions are calculated, namely the rated operating conditions, two-phase short-circuit condition, half-magnet short-circuit condition and unit out-of-step condition. The calculation results show that under the four vibration response calculation conditions, the structural deformation is concentrated at the loading position of the machine pier. The dynamic displacements of the stator base section and the bottom section of the machine pier are relatively small and relatively evenly distributed. The stress concentration (or larger stress area) mainly occurs in the machine pier, and the dynamic stress in other parts of the plant is small. It is said that the stress concentration in the load application point and its nearby area is obvious. The displacement of the unit structure in all directions, the maximum root mean square velocity and the maximum root mean square acceleration value, and the vibration stress in each direction did not exceed the allowable value. The plant is safe under the vibration load of the unit.

articleTitle: Application of stochastic finite-fault method to marine earthquake : 2021 Fukushima earthquake in Japan
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The stochastic finite-fault method is widely used to the broadband ground motion simulation for seismic engineering with the characteristics of not relying on fine underground wave velocity structure, less undetermined parameter and fast calculation speed. In this study, we take the 2011 Fukushima earthquake in Japan sea area as a study case, and adapt the stochastic finite-fault approach to simulate KiK-net borehole station. The study showed the results simulation by stochastic finite-fault method are small for stations near the fault but high for stations located on the land boundary. However, the simulated pseudo-acceleration response spectrum (PSA) has a residual close to 0 in the frequency ranging from 0.1 to 10 Hz, indicating that the method is effective in an average sense for the land ground motion simulation in marine earthquake. In addition, the simulation results were also compared with the Ground Motion Prediction Equation (GMPE) of BC-Hydro subduction zone in terms of ground motion characteristics, such as PSA and PGA. It is found that the predicted values by the BC-Hydro GMPE are significantly lower than observed values and the difference trend between them is basically a constant at high frequencies, indicating that the global average stress drop adopted in the GMPE is small when it is applied to the Fukushima earthquake, Japan. Overall, this study provides a reference to the application of stochastic finite-fault method in marine earthquake and to the development of corresponding ground motion prediction equations.

articleTitle: Using modified biochar as a physical-chemical conditioner for waste activated sludge dewatering
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The development of safe, efficient, environmentally friendly and cheap skeleton particles is a hot spot in the study of sludge reduction and resource utilization in the field of environmental engineering in my country. In this study, we prepared for the first time a biochar P-BC modified with polyaluminum chloride as a physical and chemical conditioning agent to be used in the field of sludge dewatering. The sludge moisture content, sludge specific resistance, and sludge compressibility coefficient are used to evaluate the sludge dewatering effect of P-BC. When the dosage of P-BC is 1.25 g/gTSS, WC drops to 79.65±3%, and SRF drops to 7.73±0.1×10<sup>12</sup> m/kg, indicating that the sludge dewatering performance has been significantly improved. Through analysis of changes in Zeta potential, sludge particle size and distribution of extracellular polymer components before and after sludge pretreatment, the mechanism of P-BC promotion of sludge dewatering was explored, and it was proved that P-BC can neutralize sludge. The negative charge in the sludge promotes the agglomeration of sludge particles, promotes the conversion of the bound water inside the EPS to free water, and effectively improves the sludge dewatering effect.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation for liquefaction mitigation of saturated sand stratum reinforced by fiber
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Fiber reinforcement effectively mitigates the liquefaction of saturated sand, which is confirmed by experiments. However, it is still unclear that the liquefaction mitigation effect of the reinforced saturated sand stratum. This study investigates the liquefaction mitigation of saturated sand stratum reinforced by fiber through finite element (FE) numerical simulation. Firstly, a series of strain-controlled cyclic triaxial tests are conducted, and the triaxial test is modeled using open-source computational platform OpenSees. The constitutive model parameters of reinforced sand are calibrated based on the results of finished cyclic triaxial test. Then, a two-dimensional FE model of saturated sand stratum is created using the calibrated constitutive model parameters for different reinforced sands. Finally, the dynamic analysis is performed based on the created FE model, and the liquefaction mitigation of different reinforced sand strata is explored under earthquake excitation. The results show that fiber reinforcement plays an important role in mitigating pore water pressure and liquefaction-induced displacement in the sand stratum, and liquefaction mitigation effect increases with increasing fiber content. The investigation results will provide a valuable reference for the numerical simulation and engineering application of the liquefaction mitigation of reinforced saturated sand stratum.

articleTitle: The effect of freezing on wind erosion amount under different soil moisture
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to explore the effect of freezing on wind erosion of the Yellow River in Ulan Buh Desert section, in frozen and unfrozen state, taking dry sand as contrast, prepared different soil water content (2%, 4%, 6%), analysed the amount of wind erosion and water loss under different soil moisture in the two periods. The results showed that: (1) Whether frozen or unfrozen state, wind erosion decreased with soil moisture, the wind erosion and water loss were in the order of CK $\gt 2$% $\gt 4$% $\gt 6$%, that soil moisture inhibit wind erosion, and the soil moisture was higher, the degree of inhibition was more obvious. (2)In comparison with frozen soil and unfrozen state, soil erosion decreased with the increase of soil moisture, but the effect of wind erosion was more obvious under the frozen soil, it reduced by 2.6%-25.6%. When the soil moisture content reached 6%, the difference was not significant. Under the same initial water content, there is no significant difference in water loss rate between frozen and unfrozen state. Sand dune soil freezes, forming a relatively stable frozen layer on the soil surface, enhancing the soil erosion resistance. The formation of soil frozen layer on the sand dune surface in winter can effectively reduce sand dune wind erosion and preserve the soil moisture in the frozen layer of sand dune.

articleTitle: Nonlinear numerical analysis of composite foundation with variable cross-section screw compaction piles
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Screw pile is a new type of special-shaped pile, which has the advantages of high efficiency, environmental protection and economy. At present, there is no accurate understanding of the failure mode of screw pile composite foundation. For a material warehouse variable cross-section compacted screw pile composite foundation, when the material is piled up to a height of 5m-6m, the ground subsides, the maximum subsidence is about 1.30m, the grid column has a large deformation, and the maximum horizontal displacement reaches 680mm. Establish a calculation model of variable cross-section compact screw pile composite foundation, analyze the deformation and failure of the composite foundation, and analyze the influence of the pile foundation of the side column of the material warehouse. Numerical simulation results show that the plastic zone appears under the piled load, and the cross section is close to a semicircle; with the increase of the piled load, the slip surface of the foundation becomes more and more obvious, and the position of the slip surface is within 25m to the right of the stacking center. And the safety factor is getting lower and lower; the maximum horizontal displacement of the rigid composite pile appears at a distance of 8m from the ground.

articleTitle: Shaking table model tests of composite reinforcement aseismic measure for high earth rockfill dam and its application
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The seismic safety of high earth rockfill dam is a prominent problem in hydropower development in strong earthquake area of Western China. Based on a summary of advantages and disadvantages of previous aseismic measures for high earth rockfill dam, a patented technology on the composite reinforcement aseismic measure (abbr. CRAM) for high earth rockfill dam was invented by the authors. In order to verify the aseismic effect of the CRAM, the comparative model tests were carried out by large-scale shaking table. The results showed that the CRAM had an inhibition effect on the acceleration response; the CRAM can suppress effectively the loosening and sliding of rockfill at the dam crest, and decrease the earthquake-induced permanent deformation. With the increase of the input peak acceleration, the effect of the CRAM was more obvious on decreasing the residual dam crest settlement. Finally, the engineering application of the CRAM in the aseismic design of Lianghekou gravelly soil core rockfill dam with a dam height of 295 m in China was introduced.

articleTitle: Research on the application of new generation information technology in safety monitoring of watershed hub operation
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The traditional safety monitoring system can no longer meet the needs of smart watershed and smart dam construction. In order to realize the safety monitoring of the operation the dam of watershed hub, three aspects including global intelligent perception, modular intelligent management and digital intelligent service are proposed in this paper. Based on these aspects, safety monitoring system of watershed hub operation and its function realization are deployed, and research studies on its new generation of information technology are conducted, which lays the foundation for the application of the new generation of information technology to the safety monitoring system.

articleTitle: Experimental study on mechanical properties of weak interface of rammed earth structure
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Under the action of an earthquake, the rammed earth structure will produce shear failure due to insufficient shear strength. This damage is more serious at the weak interface of each rammed earth layer. In order to study the shear strength of each weak interface, through large-scale direct shear tests, the effects of different modification ratios and sheet roughness on the shear strength, cohesion, internal friction angle and failure morphology of each weak interface were studied. The results of the study show that the addition of modified materials can significantly increase the shear strength of the rammed earth-rammed earth interface. Under different normal pressures, 15% cement has the best lifting effect, but it has the best resistance to rammed earth and building boards. The shear strength has little effect; The shear strength at the interface between the rammed earth and the plate is also affected by the normal pressure, the surface roughness of the plate and the strength of the rammed earth material; The curing agent is significantly improved by improving the bonding effect between particles. The shear strength at the interface of the rammed layer is not obvious, but the influence on the angle of internal friction is not obvious.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Stochastic Damage on Main Dike of Yangtse Rive
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The study focuses on the fuzzy stochastic damage behaviors of Jingnan Main Dike of Yangtze River. The advanced mathematical model and numerical algorithm are developed comprehensively. Moreover, the creation of model and algorithm is applied in the investigation on the behaviors of Jingnan Main Dike of Yangtze River. The generalized damage mechanics on the complicated engineering system is studied successfully.

articleTitle: Effect of rubber particles on properties of abrasion resistant concrete
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The rubber particles have good elasticity and can be used to improve the toughness of concrete to absorb energy, and have the potential to be used to make abrasion resistant concrete. In this paper, the compressive and tensile strength of concretes with different fineness and different dosage of rubber particles were studied, and the abrasion resistance of those concretes were also studied by the underwater method, high-speed underwater method, rotary jet method and drop-weight test method. The results showed that rubber particles, replacing sand at the same volume, made the mobility of concretes worse and the compressive strength and direct tensile strength of concretes decreased, but the ultimate tensile value increased significantly, and the elastic modulus decreased markedly. Rubber particles can improve the resistance of concrete to abrasion erosion and impact of high speed flow with sands or stones. Rubber particles can improve the abrasion resistance of concrete.

articleTitle: New Characteristics of the Temporal and Spatial Evolution of Urbanization in the Basin of Taihu
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Integrating the latest socio-economic statistics of cities in the Basin of Taihu and the global surface remote sensing data set, GlobeLand30, which includes the latest land cover information, it analyzes the phased characteristics of the watershed urbanization development from the perspective of time, and focused on analyzing the new characteristics in the process of urbanization in the basin from the spatial pattern of land use. The results show that: Since 1990, the urbanization of Taihu Lake Basin has shifted from a period of low-speed development to a period of medium-high-speed development, especially after 2000, the urbanization speed has accelerated significantly. The expansion of built-up land in the basin presents two characteristics. One is the expansion of the surrounding circle around the main cities, and the other is the linear expansion around the main traffic arteries or backbone rivers, which further leads to the urbanization of the eastern part of the basin. From 2000 to 2010, the absolute increase in urban area area was the largest in PDPX, where Shanghai is located. From 2010 to 2020, as the level of urbanization in Shanghai gradually becomes saturated, the absolute growth of urban area in the four regions of HJH, WCXY, YCDM, and HX exceeds that of PDPX. The urban area growth center of the basin has been transferred from Shanghai to other second-tier cities in the basin.

articleTitle: Virtual Design of Submarine Transportation Device
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The study focuses on the virtual design of the submarine wheel device that can transport the marine resources as well as the pertinent equipments. The hydro-dynamic environment where the submarine wheel device works has been simulated with the finite element analysis. The FEM in the study has been developed based on the submarine kinematic algorithm. The specific structure parameters have been offered to establish the virtual model of the submarine wheel device and the comprehensive working behaviors have been investigated with the developed finite element methodology. The study also discusses the key point on the optimized design of the submarine wheel device.

articleTitle: Study on Periodic Self-excited Vibration Process of Top Water Seal for High Head Valve with Small Opening
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: During the opening and closing process of high-head ship lock valve, the top water seal will produce self-excited vibration under the condition of small opening, even lead to strong vibration and cavitation damage of the valve. Furthermore, affect the safety and efficiency of navigation buildings. Through the combination of experiment and numerical simulation, the non harmonic periodic self-excited vibration of top water seal is studied in this paper. With each vibration cycle divided into three stages, the variation law of fluctuating pressure and VOF and opening are analyzed in each stage, and it is found that the gap flow cavitation plays an important role in self-excited vibration of the the valve water seal, which is helpful to the in-depth understanding of strong self-excited vibration of the high-head valve.

articleTitle: Uncertainty evaluation model of embankment safety based on monitoring and detection data fusion
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Embankment is an important water retaining structure and an important part of ensuring flood control safety. The traditional method of embankment safety and stability evaluation usually puts forward the stability early warning value for a single monitoring data, trying to find out the correlation between stability and monitoring data from a statistical point of view, which may get a one-sided evaluation conclusion, and also does not make full use of the existing monitoring and detection data information. Based on Bayesian theory, a monitoring and detection information fusion model integrating structural analysis, data mining, and comprehensive prediction is established. Based on structural analysis and considering the overall stability of the embankment, the forward analysis and inverse analysis fusion platform of detected monitoring are built, and the data mining model is constructed by response surface method, it avoids large-scale and cumbersome structural analysis and calculation. An engineering case is selected to apply the evaluation model. The evaluation model can integrate monitoring and detection information at the same time, predict the probability density distribution of the overall stability of the embankment, capture abnormal data, and evaluate the safety state of the embankment, which provides beneficial support for the management decision of the embankment.

articleTitle: Research on the Calculation Method of the Settlement of Hydraulic Filling of Soil Mass
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In the dredger fill project, there is a large error in the estimation of the settlement of the dredger fill, and it is of great significance to select a reasonable method to calculate and predict the settlement of the dredger fill. The fluid-solid coupling numerical analysis model is established by PLAXIS based on the finite element method to simulate the layered filling construction process of dredger fill, analyze the change law of consolidation and settlement of dredger fill, and analyze the calculation results with those of the traditional engineering design by layer-wise summation method (LSM) and the settlement curve fitting method. The above example of the dredger reclamation project in the Hengsha 8th period 1# enclosure of the beach reclamation project is verified. The research results show that the calculation of the dredger fill settlement based on the finite element method and the estimated dredger fill settlement is more reasonable. The minimum difference with the measured result is 7mm; it can provide a reliable basis for the design and construction of similar projects.

articleTitle: Research on the small strain stiffness behavior of soft clay under complex stress path
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: A series of principal stress rotation tests were carried out on soft clay with a hollow cylinder apparatus equipped with high censers. Stress paths with various principal stress directions were conducted. The influence of intermediate principal stress parameter (b) and shear stress level (q) was taken into consideration. The effect of stress rotation on the small strain stiffness of soft clay was studied in particular. The test results indicated that, the stiffness of soft clay was affected by the magnitude of strain under complex stress condition. The stiffness was relatively higher when strain was smaller than 0.01%, and the stiffness decreased quickly during 0.01%~0.1%. The influence of shearing direction on the small strain stiffness was unobvious, while the influence of b was obvious.

articleTitle: Comparison of Actual Engineering Effects of Heat of Hydration Inhibitor on Mass Concrete with Different Thickness
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The concrete hydration heat inhibitor can inhibit the early hydration reaction of concrete and reduce the initial heat release of concrete. At present, there are no actual comparative results on the effect of heat of hydration inhibitors on hydraulic structures with different thickness and constraints. Taking a large-volume concrete wall in a large pumping station structure as the research object, the effect of passing water in pipe and adding concrete inhibitor on delaying and reducing temperature peak of concrete wall with different thickness was compared and analyzed by field test. The results show that for structures with thickness less than 1.3m, adding inhibitors without other cooling measures just can control the peak temperature of concrete, but only adding inhibitors can’t achieve the optimal control of temperature drop rate. The results can provide reference for the engineering application of heat of hydration inhibitors in the future.

articleTitle: Research on Grouting Support of Large Pipe Shed Based on the Principle of ADECO-RS Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Choosing a suitable shallow-buried asymmetric tunnel entrance construction plan is the first step in tunnel construction. This paper takes Georgia’s E60 highway 3.0.04-AT tunnel T opening as an engineering case. Two opening construction schemes with or without advanced pipe shed support based on the principle of ADECO-RS approach are compared. The results show that: (1) The pipe roof pre-support can promote the formation of stress arches, improve the force of the advanced core soil and reduce the extrusion deformation; (2) Within the range of about 1 times the hole diameter of the tunnel face, the rate of settlement of the vault is the largest, and the amount of deformation reaches about 80% of the total deformation; (3) The pipe roof pre-support greatly reduces the plastic zone of the surrounding rock and avoids the plastic zone of the surrounding rock at the entrance of the cave from developing to the surface and causing the cave entrance to collapse. Finally, it can be concluded that the use of pipe roof pre-support at the entrance of the tunnel can greatly improve the stability of the surrounding rock and ensure the safety of the tunnel.

articleTitle: Design and research of tower-pier of high head Hydropower Station – Take Mujiajia hydropower station as an example
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The ballast pier is an important hydraulic structure of high head diversion hydropower station. Its function is to completely fix the pressure steel pipe and bear various axial forces on the pipe, and the pipe is not allowed to produce displacement and rotation in any direction. The safety of the ballast pier is directly related to the safety of the power station. The design of pier should be based on the design of pier shape, the anti-sliding stability and foundation stress of pier should be checked, and the volume of pier should be reduced as much as possible to reduce the project cost under the condition of satisfying the safety. Based on the analysis of pier design of Mujiajia-grade 1 hydropower station, this paper summarizes the design ideas of pier design of Gaositou hydropower station, hoping to be helpful to pier design of similar hydropower stations.

articleTitle: Study on the Response of Rice Yield and Water Consumption to Climate Change in the South China—A case study of the Nanliujiang Catchment
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Rice growth is very sensitive to climate factors such as precipitation, air temperature and carbon dioxide concentration. The change in the global climate has potential risks to rice production and agricultural irrigation in the South China. In this study, the SWAT model is used to analyse the changes of rice yield and water consumption in the Nanliujiang Catchment in Guangxi Province. A method of subbasin delineation is used for the model setup to reflect the differences between irrigation areas in yield and water use of rice, and the simulation values of rice yield, evapotranspiration and runoff are validated. Finally, the outputs of HadGEM2-ES under three RCPs (RCP2.6, RCP 4.5, RCP 8.5) are fed to the SWAT model to study the effects of future climate change on rice yield and water consumption in the Nanliujiang Catchment. The results showed that the SWAT model is an ideal tool to simulate rice growth and water consumption; the yield of irrigated rice under three RCPs decreased by 2.3%, 0.67% and 3.4%, respectively, and the yield of rain-fed rice decreased by 2.7%, 1.0% and 3.7%, respectively. Under the three RCPs, the production water consumption of irrigated rice is reduced by 4.5%, 4.6% and 6.9%, respectively, and that of rain-fed rice is reduced by 3.6%, 2.5% and 5.1%, respectively. This study can provide a scientific basis for the formulation of relevant policies to cope with future climate change in the study area.

articleTitle: Anti-overturning analysis of in-situ jacking foundation for 500KV high voltage transmission tower
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Taking the 500 kV double-circuit transmission line jacking project as the background, aiming at the overturning phenomenon that may occur in the foundation of the high-voltage transmission tower jacking process, the finite element software is used to establish a three-tower six-line tower-line coupling system calculation model, considering the wires Numerical analysis of wind load response, self-weight effect of transmission tower, and tower-line coupling tension. The research results show that the y-direction bending moment value of each independent foundation will be significantly changed after the jacking, and the y-direction bending moment value of the sole base No. 2 will have a greater increase. In addition, the y-direction bending moment values of the upper and lower connecting beams cast in-situ after the transmission tower is lifted will suddenly increase, indicating that when the high-voltage transmission tower is lifted in situ, each foundation must be strengthened to avoid longitudinal restraints at the bottom of the foundation. Sudden instability of bending moment.

articleTitle: Development of intelligent integrated design system for hydraulic plane steel gate
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In this paper, the parametric programming language APDL of structural analysis software ANSYS and python object-oriented intelligent interface development tool pyqt5 are used to develop the intelligent integrated design system of plane steel gate. The system is composed of three parts. In the first part, the preliminary design module of plane gate based on design specification is developed by python. In the second part, APDL parametric language is used to build the database of gate components, loads, constraints and other parameters, and the three-dimensional finite element model of the overall gate is established. In the third part, the finite element structural calculation is carried out by using ANSYS software. According to the finite element calculation results, further optimization analysis is carried out to optimize the component parameters and optimize the stress state of the gate. In these parts, pyqt5 interface development tool, APDL parametric programming language and the powerful structural analysis function of ANSYS are integrated. The visual interface is used for integrated design. The data transmission of the three parts is seamlessly connected through the developed interface module, forming an intelligent and integrated plane steel gate design system, which greatly improves the design quality and design efficiency.

articleTitle: Mechanical Analysis of ditch conduit using discrete-continuous coupling method
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The analysis of load-bearing ditch conduit is conducted using the discrete-continuous coupling method at the macroscopic and mesoscopic scales. To better reflect the uneven settlement between the undisturbed soil and the filling soil, the undisturbed soil is meshed by grids, and the filling soil is modeled by pellets. The mesoscopic parameters used for particle flow simulation are given through calibration. The results show that the settlements of soils reach maximum at the top of the conduit. Under the ground load, the conduit has a horizontal expansion. The process of loading can be reconstructed by the observation of the force chain structure. The relationship between the deformation of the conduit and the movement of the pellets shows that the structure of force chain can give a good explanation for the mechanism of force transfer.

articleTitle: Air-void optimization of self compacting concrete
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The air-void of self compacting concrete (SCC) with different mix proportions is studied, considering the influence of sand ratio, fly ash and admixtures. The flow test and air content test were conducted and furthermore the hardened SCCs were cut and the images of the cross sections were taken with the aim of investigating their internal pore characteristics. The results of SCC workability test were consistent with those indicated by images. The higher the flow was, the lower the air content was and the less the pore numbers were. Sand ratio and admixtures were the most important factors which affected the SCC pore characteristic. Within a certain range, the decrease of sand ration could increase the flowability of SCC and reduce the pore numbers. The admixtures, water reducer and defoamer, also had a same effect of air-void decrease, while the effect of defoamer was not significant.

articleTitle: Study on deformation and force of a super high arch dam during impoundment period in Southwest China
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Based on the prototype monitoring results of a super high arch dam during the impoundment period in Southwest China, this paper systematically analyzes and researches the existing monitoring results, preliminarily evaluates the operation status of the dam during impoundment period, and better demonstrates the performance of different monitoring instruments through the QH3D software monitoring results. The results are compared with the three-dimensional finite element results, and the mechanism of stress and deformation of an extra-high arch dam in southwest China during impoundment is studied in depth. This study can find the potential risk of the dam in time, and give early warning of the serious problems such as cracks in the dam body and key parts.

articleTitle: The In-depth BIM-based Application of Hypergravity Centrifugal Simulation and Experimental Equipment Project
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In the project of supergravity centrifugal simulation and experimental device, the BIM application is carried out throughout the process in order to improve the construction quality. In this paper, a hyper-gravity BIM platform is developed, and 3d collaborative design results are published on the web in light weight. Combining the requirements of the project application, this paper sorts out the relationship among the 3D model, design files, and technical disclosure, develops design clarification and design data management modules, which practices in deepening the application of BIM. With the help of this hyper-gravity BIM platform, online technical disclosure and design file management based on lightweight BIM are realized for the first time, forming complete BIM-oriented design data assets. The practical results are of great significance for promoting the application of BIM and improving the quality of project construction.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Stress and the Deformation Characteristics of the Initial Support of the Large Section deeply buried in the sandy loess tunnel
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: To explore the stress and deformation characteristics of a large section that deeply buried in the sandy loess tunnel structure, numerical simulation and field test analysis were carried out and the initial support structure of sandy loess tunnel was studied based on the Panxian Mountain Tunnel Project in Zhonglankezhuan. With field sand loess physical parameter and mechanical properties, a series of numerical simulation of complex was calculated, the scene actual situation was highly restored, and the steel arch bending moment, axial force and the tunnel vault settlement were calculated. Then, the stress characteristics of the initial support of the tunnel are analyzed by using the time-varying curve and the distribution nephogram in the final state. At the same time, according to the field monitoring steel arch strain, its stress characteristics were analyzed. The stress was then converted into internal force from material mechanics that verify the reliability of the numerical simulation results. The research can provide some help for the subsequent researches and construction of sandy loess tunnel, with a certain reference significance.

articleTitle: Influence analysis and safety assessment of vehicle bomb type on the dynamic response of curved bridge under bridge deck blast load : ——(II): Safety assessment
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In this study, to determine the dynamic response and failure mode of curved girder bridge under bridge deck explosion loading, a four-span curved continuous box girder bridge in a ramp bridge is adopted as the engineering background. The finite element models of curved girder bridge, and air were built. Given the strain response of each component of the bridge under blast, the safety assessment was conducted on component, part, unit and bridge structure through an analytic hierarchy. As revealed from the results, the safety effect of different blasts follows the order of car bomb < minibus car bomb < van bomb < truck bomb. When tank bomb explodes, the whole span of curved bridge deck collapses.

articleTitle: Deformation Prediction Method of Deep Foundation Pit Support Structure Based On GA-BP
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Aiming at the low prediction quantile of the traditional deformation prediction method of deep foundation pit support structure, a deformation prediction method of deep foundation pit support structure based on GA-BP is designed. Through the field measured deformation information of deep foundation pit retaining structure, the deformation element grid of deep foundation pit retaining structure is divided, the time fractal characteristics of deep foundation pit retaining structure deformation structure are analyzed, and the deformation prediction mapping error of deep foundation pit retaining structure is calculated based on the training data of GA-BP algorithm, so as to realize the deformation prediction of deep foundation pit retaining structure. The experimental results show that the fractal dimension of the designed prediction method is significantly higher than that of the control group, which can solve the problem of low prediction quantile of the traditional deformation prediction method of deep foundation pit support structure.

articleTitle: Identification and risk assessment of a dangerous rock mass in high-steep slope based on 3D laser scanning
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The boundary of a dangerous rock mass is controlled by the structures of rock masses, and the structural plane information can be obtained through 3D laser point clouds, which provides a data basis for risk assessments. This paper first introduces the principle of terrestrial 3D laser scanning, as well as the identification and interpretation methods of rock mass structural planes. Aiming at a high-steep slope on the left bank of a hydropower station, the location of a unstable rock mass is accurately identified based on 3D point cloud data, and its geometric dimensions and controllable structural plane occurrence are measured. The instability process of the rock mass is simulated using discrete elements, and the results show that the movement has experienced five stages: plane sliding, free falling, collision bouncing, rolling, continuous rebound until static. The maximum speed of the falling rock can reach 84.26 m/s, and the maximum bounce height and horizontal distance are 30m and 40m respectively, posing a great threat to the safety of structures and personnel during construction. This research can provide references to the identification and hazard risk assessment of dangerous rock masses on high-steep slopes.

articleTitle: Risk Assessment of Urban Earthquake Prevention Based on Intelligent Multiple Attribute Decision Making Model
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Urban earthquake disaster prevention system is a complex open giant system including many factors such as the hazard factors, bearing bodies, hazard-formative environments and damaged conditions, which has the features of highly nonlinear, complexity and spatial dynamic. In this thesis, on the basis of “competition view optimization” and “fuzzy linguistic quantification”, a risk evaluation model based on the fuzzy set theory and multiple attribute decision making theory is proposed, which has been verified by the related definition and theoretical analysis. Firstly, we refined the risk assessment indexes and control factors of earthquake disaster based on the aspects of disaster prevention space, land use function, disaster bearing body and secondary disaster, in this procedure, the risk indicators also has been quantitative fuzzy processed by fuzzy set theory. Furthermore, the Weighted Particle Swarm optimization (WPSO) algorithm is used to calculate the average weight value of risk evaluation index combined with “Weights non-dictatorship condition”. Then, we made a thorough description of this model in order to comparative with Entropy Weight-Topsis evaluation model and Self-Determination model. Finally, an example is given to illustrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the Intelligent Multiple Attribute Decision Making model.

articleTitle: Shear Mechanical and Permeability Properties of Deep Rock Mass under Thermal-Hydraulic-Mechanical Coupling
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: For the deep fractured rock mass, a variety of factors determine its mechanical properties, such as high in-situ stress, high seepage pressure and high temperature, etc. A series of shear experiments on saturated sandstone under different normal stress, seepage pressures were carried out, which had conducted five heat-water treatments. The setting max temperatures were 100, 300 and 400°C. The seepage pressure is constantly selected to be 5 MPa, while the normal stresses are 10, 15, and 20 MPa, respectively. The shear-seepage characteristics of sandstone under hydraulic-mechanical coupling were studied. The peak shear stress and its corresponding peak shear deformation increase with the increase of normal stress; with the increase of normal stress, the shear strength of specimen increases nearly nonlinearly. With the increase of temperature and water seepage pressure, the shear strength and the corresponding peak shear deformation will decrease. The weakening effect of seepage pressure on its shear mechanics was analysed. The study can provide a scientific theoretical basis for rock strength damage mechanism and disaster control under thermal-hydraulic-mechanical coupling in deep rock engineering.

articleTitle: Experimental study on seismic performance of the beam with openings of subway station
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Based on the research on the key components of one prefabricated subway station in Guangzhou, this paper designed and conducted the seismic performance tests on the reference beam (no openings) and the beam with openings. During the cyclic loading tests, the hysteresis curves, cracking pattern and skeleton curves are analyzed and discussed. The results show that both beams demonstrated promising ductility. Moreover, the existence of openings does weaken the seismic performance of the beam, but dense reinforcement besides the opening could effectively retard the emergence and development of cracks. As the concrete strength level increases from C40 to C60, the finite element analysis could provide a reliable way to conduct parametric analysis. The research conclusions can provide reference basis and related design guidance for the application of opening beams in subway station structures.

articleTitle: Analysis of Spatial and Temporal Variation of the NDVI in the Upper Reaches of the Heihe River from 2001-2017
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Vegetation is an important part of terrestrial ecosystem, and the change of vegetation cover can reflect the change of regional environment, and the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) can effectively reflect the growth status of vegetation. In this study, based on Moderate-resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) NDVI data from 2001 - 2017 in the upper reaches of the Heihe River, we analyzed the spatial and temporal variation characteristics of the NDVI in the upper reaches of the Heihe River for 17 years using spatial autocorrelation analysis method, trend analysis, accumulative anomaly method and Pettitt mutation test method. The results showed that the spatial distribution of the NDVI in the upper reaches of the Heihe River was high in the southeast and low in the northwest, and the spatial trend was increasing in the northwest and decreasing in the southeast; the mean values of the NDVI from 2001 to 2017 showed an overall increasing trend with an increase rate of 0.0017/a and the NDVI changed abruptly around 2009-2010. This study contributes to a better understanding of vegetation cover changes in the upper reaches of the Heihe River, which is important for ecological conservation in the upper reaches of the Heihe River.

Author Keywords: upper reaches of the Heihe River

articleTitle: Evaluation of bridge health status based on multi-source data fusion of monitoring and inspection
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: In order to study the evaluation method of bridge health state, a continuous rigid frame bridge was taken as the engineering background, and a multi-source data fusion system of continuous rigid frame bridge was constructed by comparing and analyzing three data fusion methods. Based on the research of data-level fusion method, the health monitoring system of continuous rigid frame bridge was established. Based on the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and the big data of bridge supervision and inspection, the health status of the bridge was evaluated according to the order of sub-components, components and the whole structure of the bridge. By comparing the evaluation result with the current standard, it is found that the evaluation result of this method is closer to the engineering practice.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Sediment Model in the Reservoir Area of Upper Arun Hydroelectric Station in Nepal
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Nepal is rich in water resources, but the installed capacity and power generation in the country are far below the power demand of basic load and peak load. Therefore, Nepal Electricity Authority launched the Upper Arun Hydroelectric Project with financial aid from the World Bank. The Upper Arun Hydroelectric Station has the characteristics of “high productive head, small reservoir capacity, large sediment concentration and high sediment hardness” and its reservoir sediment dispatching mode and the layout of the upstream nosing engineering buildings have been highly concerned by the World Bank’s hydropower experts and project design team. This paper, using the method of the combination of one-dimensional numerical simulation and physical model test, studies and analyzes issues such as the sediment deposit amount, deposit elevation and deposit distribution of the reservoir, desilting efficiency of desilting tunnel, sediment flushing effect of emptying discharge of reservoir and sediment characteristics of power station passing through the turbine, etc. The layout of hydroproject and the operation mode of reservoir sediment dispatching is verified or optimized.

articleTitle: Mountainous flood risk analysis and mapping in riverside town based on geographic information system and hydraulic model
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The flood risk assessment of riverside town based on hydraulic model is of great significance for flood disaster prevention and engineering treatment. The paper starts with river system distribution and flood source analysis in case study of Tongcheng County, Hubei Province. In addition, a flood calculation and analysis program is proposed. The typical frequency (0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10 and 0.20) of flood routing and inundation process are calculated based on TUFLOW software to obtain more accurate flood inundation range, inundation depth and other information. Combined with GIS, urban flood risk mapping is carried out. The calculation results show that the technical method proposed in this paper is feasible. The main sections of the main stream of Junshui River in Tongcheng County meet the flood control standard of 20-year return period, and the current flood control capacity of some sections of Xiushui River is rather low.

articleTitle: Study on Environmental Factor Analysis and Fragility Zoning of Road Water Damage by Using ArcGIS
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Taking environmental factors for road water damage as research object, the multi-attribute decision-making method was adopted to build the factor system of fragility evaluation, including 6 environmental factors: terrain, land surface slope, geomorphic type, drainage density, geological disaster development along road and vegetation cover. Combined with ArcGIS, five fragility grades were divided as slight fragility, low fragility, middle fragility, high fragility and extreme fragility, and the spatial distribution of fragility grades corresponding to each environmental factor was drawn. Delphi method was used to analyze and to assign values to six environmental factors. Analytic Hierarchy Process and expert opinion correction method were used to determine the weight of each environmental factor. Based on the multi-factor comprehensive index method, the fragility zoning calculation model was constructed and the environment of road water damage was classified and zoned according to the calculated threshold. The research results are consistent with the actual situation, which provides important scientific basis and practical significance for road disaster prevention and mitigation.

articleTitle: Influence of Orifice Plates on Taylor Bubble of Geyser in Storage Tunnel System
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The storage tunnel system is an important project to solve the shortage of urban storage capacity and prevent waterlogging, geyser phenomenon is a serious hydraulic accident in the system, and it is of great significance to study geyser characteristics and flow control measures for safe operation of storage tunnel system. In the present work, the bubble rising process in the vertical pipe was studied used numerical simulation method, the influence of orifice plates on Taylor bubble of geyser in storage tunnel system had been analyzed in detail. The research results indicated that orifice plates had a significant effect on Taylor bubble of geyser, under the action of orifice plates, the bubble shape, bubble pressure and flow field structure are fundamentally changed due to the influence of local jet flow and entrainment air, the difference value between the bubble pressure head and the water column height and the pressure gradient of water column were greatly reduced, which leaded to a significant reduction of the bubble rising height and the maximum bubble velocity, this was beneficial to reduce the intensity of geyser in storage tunnel system.

articleTitle: Settlement Analysis of Pool Foundation Near the Slope Excavation
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The excavation of a slope will break the balance of the soil and make the soil deform to the free face. If there are structures on the top of the slope, the safety of the structures will be affected. To study the settlement characteristics and laws of the foundation of the adjacent pool structure in the process of slope excavation, the numerical simulation method was used to simulate the construction process, and the settlement characteristics of the foundation of the pool structure under the influence of the adjacent slope excavation were obtained. The results show that after the anti-slide pile construction and soil excavation are completed, the ground surface settlement curve behind the pile is “ √ ” shape and the maximum ground surface settlement is -10.76 mm. During construction, the foundation settlement value on the east side of the pool structure is generally greater than that on the west side, and the settlement value on the north side is generally greater than that on the south side. The maximum additional settlement of the pool structure is -9.51 mm, and the maximum additional overall inclination value is 0.21 %∘. The maximum additional settlement of the foundation of the pool structure is located at the southeast corner of the structure, and the maximum inclination value is at the south side of the pool structure along the width direction. The maximum settlement value is less than 10 mm, the inclination value is generally small, and the structure is relatively safe. The settlement deformation of the pool foundation near the excavation side mainly occurs in the anti-slide pile construction stage, and the settlement deformation of the pool foundation far away from the excavation site mainly occurs in the soil excavation stage. In different stages of the construction process, the monitoring of structural foundation settlement shall be strengthened, and the foundation settlement value and inclination value shall be strictly controlled to ensure the safety of structures during the construction process.

articleTitle: Experimental study on expansion performance of ultra-high performance concrete
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The expansion performance of ultra-high performance concrete (UHPC) is experimentally studied, and the influence of expansion agent on the expansion performance of UHPC is analyzed. The results show that type FP expansive agent can significantly improve the expansion performance of UHPC in the early hardening stage (3 hours). Type II expansive agent can significantly improve the later expansion performance of UHPC (3 hours to 24 hours). The combination of the two can meet the expansion performance index of UHPC required by the project. The optimum content of type FP and type II expansive agent is 0.1% and 6% respectively. The research conclusions can provide basis for UHPC grouting construction.

articleTitle: Study on Seismic Isolation of Electrical Transformer by Lead Rubber Bearing
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: Electric transformer is an important part in electrical substation. In Ultra High Voltage (UHV) grid, a 1000 kV transformer is nearly 11 meters in length, 16 meters in height and 570 tons in weight. Previous seismic studies of transformer were usually conducted on those that were much lower in voltage level and smaller in geometry. This paper provides an insight into seismic performance of a 1000 kV transformer. Finite Element model was built to simulate the dynamic properties and seismic response the transformer. Isolation technique is seemed to be an economical method for seismic enhancement of transformer. In this paper, seismic isolation which makes use of lead rubber bearing is designed for the 1000 kV transformer with numerical validation. The acceleration at the bottom of transformer has been decreased and the safety margin for high voltage bushing has been elevated.

articleTitle: Study on temperature gradient of concrete box girder in Shandong area based on long-term monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The stress and deformation of concrete curved box girder bridge due to temperature are complex, but the climatic conditions in different regions are quite different. In order to study the temperature gradient of concrete box girder in Shandong province, a temperature monitoring system was installed in a bridge for long-term continuous monitoring. Based on the analysis of massive monitoring data by mathematical statistics, the temperature distribution of concrete box girder transverse to top and bottom and vertical to box girder in summer and winter are obtained. On this basis, a temperature gradient function of concrete curved box girder suitable for Shandong area is proposed. The results can provide a reference for the design of concrete curved box girder bridges in areas close to Shandong province in terms of climate conditions and the formulation of relevant codes.

articleTitle: Steel of Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: With the increased demands for prolonged life service of the superstructures, the durability of concrete erections is of great concern to the developers, and among the key factors that lead to concrete degradation, apparently, the corrosion is on the top list. The use of steel in such constructions have increased over time owing to a number of factors such as its lightweight, resistance to corrosion and the capacity to take any form. The use of stainless-steel reinforcements (SSRs) in the construction of the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge has proved its essence and effectiveness in ensuring the durability of the superstructure erected in the marine environment. Despite its first use in Chinese Mainland, the stainless-steel reinforcements have been employed over years across the world.

articleTitle: Study on Vibration under the Water Pulsation of the High Head Pumped Storage Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2021 7th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering & Smart Water Conservancy and Intelligent Disaster Reduction Forum (ICHCE & SWIDR)
abstract: The pump turbine of the pumped storage power station has the characteristics of high head, large capacity, high unit speed, two-way flow operation and frequent condition change, which leads to the prominent vibration problem. The rated head of a pumped storage power station is 710m, and the underground powerhouse is equipped with two kinds of pump turbines with different speeds (the rated speeds are 500r / min and 600r / min respectively). The rated head and the rated speed of 600r/min are the highest in domestic pumped storage power stations. In order to study the vibration characteristics of the power house structure under the action of water pressure pulsation of high head and high speed unit, the finite element dynamic time history method was used to study the vibration response of the power house under the assumption of harmonic load. The results show that the larger the amplitude of pressure pulsation is, the larger the vibration is.
